## Real Estate CRM for Investors: The Complete Guide (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/real-estate-crm-guide.html

Real estate CRM for investors: the complete guide.
A real estate CRM for investors is the system that tracks every seller, property, offer and buyer and makes sure no lead is forgotten. This guide covers how to choose one, the records and stages it needs, what to automate and connect, the numbers to review weekly, compliance, and a 30-day setup plan, with links to every free tool on this site.
A real estate CRM is the system that holds every seller, property, offer and buyer, and makes sure no lead is forgotten . For investors it replaces sticky notes, spreadsheets and memory.
The parts that matter: a data model built around properties, pipeline stages with rules, automation for follow-up, integrations with your phone and lead sources, and five numbers you review every week.
This guide links every free tool, checklist and deep dive on this site, so you can build or fix your CRM in order.
Contents: What it is Do you need one Types Data model Stages Automation Follow-up Integrations Reports Compliance 30-day setup Mistakes Toolkit
What is a real estate CRM?
A CRM (customer relationship management system) is a database plus rules. For a real estate investor, the database holds sellers, properties, offers, contracts and buyers; the rules decide who calls a lead, when, and what must be captured before a lead moves forward. A real estate agent CRM is built around buyers and listings; an investor CRM is built around motivated sellers, offers and dispositions. That difference is why generic advice often doesn’t fit wholesalers.
When does an investor need a CRM?
When a lead can be forgotten and nobody notices. In practice: more than one person talks to sellers, follow-ups depend on memory, or you can’t say which list paid for your last deal. The 7-sign checklist walks through it, including what a spreadsheet still does well.
What kinds of real estate CRMs are there?
Type | Good at | Watch for
Investor-specific CRMs | Ready on day one: seller fields, stages, often calling and texting built in | Limits on custom data and reports as you grow
General CRMs (HubSpot, Pipedrive and similar) | Clean pipelines, email, easy start | Built for B2B sales; property and offer tracking is on you
Salesforce | Your own data model, deep automation, any report, large integration ecosystem | Needs setup; edition decides what’s possible
Podio and no-code tools | Flexible and cheap to start | Becomes hard to maintain; see moving off Podio
Side-by-side with sources: Salesforce vs investor CRMs · Salesforce vs Follow Up Boss · wholesaling CRM .
What records and fields should a real estate CRM have?
Record | One per | Must-have fields
Lead / Seller | Person who might sell | Lead source (picklist), phone, motivation, timeline, consent and opt-out, next follow-up date, owner
Property | Address | Address, type, beds/baths, condition, ARV, repair estimate, occupancy, list/owner status
Deal (Opportunity) | Property you’re working to contract | Stage, offer amount, MAO, contract price, closing date, exit type, dead reason
Offer | Each offer made | Amount, date, rep, status (so offers made vs signed is reportable)
Buyer | Cash buyer or fund | Buy box (zips, price range, property types), proof of funds, last deal
Campaign | List, mailer, PPC or channel | Spend, dates, channel, so cost per lead and per deal compute
Activities | Call, text, email, task | Outcome (picklist), attempt number, recording link
The full field list with picklist values is in the free CRM field kit . Definitions of every term: wholesaling CRM glossary .
What pipeline stages should a wholesaler use?
Stage | Enters when | Can’t leave without
New | Lead created | First contact attempt logged
Contacted | Talked to the seller | Timeline, reason, condition, next follow-up date
Appointment | Walkthrough or call booked | Date, address confirmed, decision makers known
Offer made | Offer sent | Offer amount, MAO, offer date
Under contract | Seller signed | Contract price, signed contract on file, closing date, title company
Marketing to buyers | Dispo started | Assignment ask, buyers sent
Assigned / Closed | Buyer signed or closed | Buyer, assignment price, fee, exit type
Dead | Any stage | Dead reason (picklist) and a re-contact date if it’s “not now”
Rules like “can’t leave without” are validation rules in Salesforce; most investor CRMs support required fields per stage too. See data quality features .
What should a real estate CRM automate?
New lead → assigned owner and a call task due within minutes. Contacting within an hour made firms nearly 7× as likely to qualify a lead .
Missed inbound call → callback task plus a text, if you have consent. Only 2% of unanswered callers leave a voicemail .
No activity in 7 days → follow-up task for the owner.
“Not now” → re-contact date and a long-term cadence, not a dead lead.
Under contract → title task, dispo alert and buyer list match.
Offer above MAO → manager approval.
Duplicate lead → alert and merge, keeping the first source.
Monday → the five KPI numbers emailed to the owner.
Examples in Salesforce: 15 automation recipes for wholesalers · 5 automations every real estate team needs .
How much follow-up does a seller lead need?
More than most teams give it. 93% of converted leads were reached by the sixth call attempt in Velocify’s 2012 data, yet half of leads in the same research were never called a second time. Build the cadence into the CRM so it doesn’t depend on memory: follow-up cadence builder · speed to lead guide · all 62 statistics .
What should a real estate CRM connect to?
Tool | Why connect it | Guide
Phone / dialer | Every call and outcome on the lead | Dialers
Texting | Texts in the same timeline; opt-outs respected | Texting and 10DLC
Lead sources | Source on every lead, through to the deal | Lead sources
E-signature | Contracts on the deal | DocuSign
Accounting | Fees invoiced and collected, reportable | QuickBooks
Everything else | Email, files, Slack, maps, scheduling | All integrations
Which numbers should an investor review every week?
Five is enough to run the business: new leads by source, speed to first contact, offers made, contracts signed, and cost per kept deal. Fall-outs come out of the count. Details and formulas: the Monday 5 · KPIs in Salesforce · pipeline dashboard · kept deal map .
Calculators: cost per deal · MAO · deal analyzer · team capacity · missed call cost .
AI on top of the CRM: Salesforce AI and Agentforce for investors .
What compliance rules affect an investor’s CRM?
Texting: app-to-person texts over 10DLC numbers in the US require brand and campaign registration, per Twilio. CTIA’s guidance calls for express written consent for marketing texts and advises against rented, sold or shared lists. Store consent and opt-out on the lead. Texting guide
Calling: keep DNC flags from your list or skip-tracing provider on the record, and make every dialer respect them.
Platform changes: Salesforce’s Open CTI, used by many dialers, reaches end of life on February 28, 2028. Dialer guide
This is not legal advice; state wholesaling and telemarketing rules vary.
How do you set up a real estate CRM in 30 days?
Week 1: Decide the model
Write your stages on one page, with the fields required to leave each one. Pick lead source values. Decide who owns which leads.
Week 2: Build and import
Create fields, stages and rules. Clean and import one list first; the Data Import Wizard handles up to 50,000 records at a time in Salesforce. Check duplicates before the rest.
Week 3: Connect and automate
Phone and texting first, then web forms and lead sources. Turn on the new-lead task, missed-call task and no-activity sweep.
Week 4: Train and measure
Train on the five things each role does daily. Start the Monday review with the five numbers. Fix the field people skip most. See getting your team to use it .
Moving from another system: CRM migration · Podio migration checklist · replacing Zapier chains .
What are the most common real estate CRM mistakes?
Mistake | Fix
Lead source typed as free text | One picklist, set automatically
Leads with no next step | Every open lead has a task with a due date
“Dead” used for “not now” | A not-now status with a re-contact date
Source lost when the lead becomes a deal | Map the source to the deal and keep it to close
Each rep with their own offer math | One MAO formula on the deal
Fall-outs counted as wins | Cancelled contracts out of campaign ROI
Calls logged in the dialer only | Outcome fields on the Salesforce record
Building everything before anyone uses it | Launch the core in 30 days, then add

Questions
What is the best CRM for real estate investors?
It depends on team size and how custom your process is. Investor-specific CRMs are fastest to start; Salesforce fits teams that need their own data model, deep automation and custom reports. Compare on data model, follow-up automation, phone integration and reporting, not feature counts.
What should a real estate investor CRM track?
Sellers with lead source and next follow-up date, properties, every offer, contracts, buyers with buy boxes, campaigns with spend, and every call and text with an outcome.
How is an investor CRM different from a realtor CRM?
A realtor CRM centers on buyers, listings and the sphere of influence. An investor CRM centers on motivated sellers, offers, contracts, dispositions to cash buyers and cost per deal by lead source.
How long does it take to set up a real estate CRM?
A usable core (stages, required fields, lead sources, phone logging and the key automations) can be live in about 30 days. Reports and extra integrations come after the team is using it.
Can a CRM help with speed to lead?
Yes. Automatic assignment and a task due within minutes for every new lead, plus a callback task for missed calls, make response time a process instead of a habit.

## Speed to Lead & Follow-Up Statistics for Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/real-estate-lead-response-statistics.html

Speed to lead & follow-up statistics for real estate investors (2026).
Speed to lead is the time between a seller reaching out and a real person responding. Below are 62 statistics on lead response, follow-up, missed calls, CRM data and the 2026 investor market, each linked to the page it came from, plus 8 widely quoted “stats” I couldn’t verify.
Jump to: Speed to lead Follow-up Missed calls CRM data 2026 market Channels Myths What it means
Lead response time (speed to lead)
Answering fast is the single most studied lever in lead conversion. The research is old, mostly outside real estate, and still consistent: minutes matter, and most companies are slow.
Statistic | Source | Sample
In an audit of 2,241 US companies, only 37% responded to a web lead within an hour. | Harvard Business Review, “The Short Life of Online Sales Leads” (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington) (2011) | 2,241 US companies sent a web-generated test lead
Companies that responded to a web lead within 30 days took an average of 42 hours. | Harvard Business Review, “The Short Life of Online Sales Leads” (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington) (2011) | 2,241 US companies sent a web-generated test lead
23% of the audited companies never responded to the web lead at all. | Harvard Business Review, “The Short Life of Online Sales Leads” (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington) (2011) | 2,241 US companies sent a web-generated test lead
Firms that contacted a lead within an hour were nearly 7 times as likely to qualify it as firms that waited even one hour longer. | Harvard Business Review, “The Short Life of Online Sales Leads” (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington) (2011) | 1.25 million leads across 29 B2C and 13 B2B companies
Those same firms were more than 60 times as likely to qualify a lead as firms that waited 24 hours or more. | Harvard Business Review, “The Short Life of Online Sales Leads” (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington) (2011) | 1.25 million leads across 29 B2C and 13 B2B companies
Calling a lead within 5 minutes instead of 30 minutes made the odds of contacting it 100 times higher. | InsideSales.com / Dr. James Oldroyd (MIT Sloan), “Lead Response Management Study” (2007) | 6 companies, 15,000+ leads, 100,000+ call attempts over 3 years
Calling within 5 minutes instead of 30 minutes made the odds of qualifying the lead 21 times higher. | InsideSales.com / Dr. James Oldroyd (MIT Sloan), “Lead Response Management Study” (2007) | 6 companies, 15,000+ leads, 100,000+ call attempts over 3 years
Waiting one hour cut the odds of contact by more than 10 times and the odds of qualification by more than 6 times. | InsideSales.com / Dr. James Oldroyd (MIT Sloan), “Lead Response Management Study” (2007) | 6 companies, 15,000+ leads, 100,000+ call attempts over 3 years
In a 2013 secret-shopper audit, 47% of companies never responded to a web-form lead. | InsideSales.com, “Annual 2014 Lead Response Report” (2014) | 9,538 companies that received a successful form submission (from 14,061 sampled)
Companies that called back took 61 hours on average to place the first call. The median was 3 hours 8 minutes. | InsideSales.com, “Annual 2014 Lead Response Report” (2014) | 2,142 companies that responded by phone
Leads converted at 8 times the rate when worked within 5 minutes than at 6 minutes or later. | InsideSales (XANT), “Lead Response Management 2021” infographic (2021) | 400+ companies, 5.7M leads, 55M+ sales activities over 3 years
Fewer than 1% of lead contact attempts happened within the first 5 minutes, and 57.1% came more than a week after the lead arrived. | InsideSales (XANT), “Lead Response Management 2021” infographic (2021) | ~30M contact attempts by 10,000+ North American users, 2018-2020
Calling a new lead within one minute raised conversion by 391% over calling later. The lift fell to 160% in the second minute. | Velocify (Leads360) lead-conversion study (2012) | ~3.5M leads, 400+ companies, H1 2012
In a secret-shopper test of 74 top US real estate brokerages, 41% never answered a website inquiry. | Roof AI, “Testing response times of the top 74 brokerages” (Test date not given) | 74 brokerages, web-form inquiry
Only 9% of those 74 brokerages (7 firms) replied within 5 minutes, and all 7 had a website chatbot. | Roof AI, “Testing response times of the top 74 brokerages” (Test date not given) | 74 brokerages, web-form inquiry
B2B buyers chose the vendor they first contacted about 80% of the time. In the main survey, 77% of buyers' first vendor conversation was with the eventual winner. | 6sense, “The B2B Buyer Experience Report for 2025” (2025) | ~4,000 B2B buyers (main n=3,744), plus a supplemental n=766
Follow-up and persistence
Most leads get one or two attempts. The data says more attempts, at better times, reach more people.
Statistic | Source | Sample
50% of leads were never called a second time. | Velocify (Leads360) study (2012) | ~3.5M leads, 400+ companies
93% of leads that converted had been reached by the sixth call attempt. | Velocify (Leads360) study (2012) | ~3.5M leads, 400+ companies
Leads that needed 7 or more calls before first contact were 45% less likely to convert than leads reached in 6 or fewer. | Velocify (Leads360) study (2012) | ~3.5M leads, 400+ companies
81% of sellers made 5 or fewer follow-up attempts on a lead. | InsideSales (XANT), “Lead Response Management 2021” (2021) | ~30M attempts, 10,000+ users, 2018-2020
Making 7 or more follow-up attempts produced 15% more connections. | InsideSales (XANT), “Lead Response Management 2021” (2021) | ~30M attempts, 10,000+ users, 2018-2020
The median number of contact attempts on an inbound web lead was 1, and the average was 2.2. | InsideSales.com, “Annual 2014 Lead Response Report” (2014) | 9,538 audited companies
Thursday was the best day to reach a lead, 49.7% better than the worst day (Tuesday). Contact rates were highest from 4-6 pm. | InsideSales / Oldroyd, “Lead Response Management Study” (2007) | 15,000+ leads, 100,000+ dials
Contact rates from 9-10 a.m. were 28.4% higher than the full-day average. | InsideSales (XANT), “Lead Response Management 2021” (2021) | ~30M attempts
Among daily cold callers, the most common connect rate was 11-20% (38% of respondents). Only 5% reported more than 30%. | HubSpot, “2025 State of Cold Calling Report” (2025) | 379 sales professionals, self-reported
Among daily cold callers, 35% said 2-5% of their calls turned into appointments, the most common answer. | HubSpot, “2025 State of Cold Calling Report” (2025) | 379 sales professionals, self-reported
Missed calls and phone answering
Sellers call. If nobody answers, almost nobody leaves a message.
Statistic | Source | Sample
On average, 26% of calls from potential customers went unanswered across industries. | Invoca press release (aggregate customer call data) (2021) | Invoca's aggregate 2021 platform data
Only 2% of callers whose calls went unanswered left a voicemail. | Invoca press release (aggregate customer call data) (2021) | Invoca's aggregate 2021 platform data
Missed-call rates reached 60% in some industries, such as professional services. | Invoca press release (aggregate customer call data) (2021) | Invoca's aggregate 2021 platform data
Missed-call rates varied by industry: 32% in healthcare, 28% in legal, 14% in home services and 9% in real estate. | CallRail small business marketing benchmark report (Business Wire release) (2025) | 1.1M de-identified conversations across 7 industries, including real estate and real estate investment
About 80% of Americans said they generally don't answer cellphone calls from unknown numbers. Only 19% said they do. | Pew Research Center, “Most Americans don't answer cellphone calls from unknown numbers” (2020) | 10,211 US adults, July 13-19, 2020
CRM data quality and selling time
A CRM only helps if the data in it is trusted and reps have time to sell.
Statistic | Source | Sample
76% of CRM users said less than half of their organization's CRM data is accurate and complete. | Validity, “The State of CRM Data Management in 2025” (2025) | 602 CRM users and admins in the US, UK and Australia

8 statistics everyone quotes that I couldn't verify
These appear on hundreds of blogs and sales decks. I traced each one and could not find a primary source, or found it was misquoted. Don't repeat them as fact.
“78% of customers buy from the company that responds first.”
Usually credited to a “Lead Connect survey” with no title, year, sample or link. No primary source found. Closest real data: in 6sense’s 2025 B2B survey, buyers chose the vendor they first contacted about 80% of the time.
“35–50% of sales go to the vendor that responds first.”
Credited to InsideSales.com, but it is not in their 2007, 2014 or 2021 studies.
“80% of sales need 5 follow-ups; 2% close on first contact.”
Credited to a “National Sales Executive Association” that VentureBeat found does not exist. Use the Velocify and InsideSales follow-up data above instead.
“44% of salespeople give up after one follow-up.”
No primary source found. Real data: half of leads were never called a second time (Velocify 2012).
“85% of callers who reach voicemail won’t call back.”
Repeated widely with no original survey. Real data: 26% of calls unanswered and only 2% of those callers left a voicemail (Invoca 2021).
“The MIT study: respond in 5 minutes and you’re 100x more likely to close.”
The 100x is the odds of contacting the lead, not closing. And it is InsideSales.com data analyzed by an MIT professor, not an MIT publication.
“The average lead response time is 47 hours.”
A misquote of HBR’s 42 hours.
“Investors buy 1 in 3 homes.”
Out of date. BatchData puts investors at 26.7% of purchases in Q2 2026; Redfin puts it at 19% in Q1 2026 using a different method. Quote one with its source.
What this means for a wholesaling team
1. Measure your own speed to lead
Every study above says minutes matter, and most companies don't know their number. Stamp the time a lead arrives and the time someone actually talks to the seller, and report the gap weekly. The speed to lead guide shows how.
2. Make the sixth attempt automatic
93% of converted leads were reached by the sixth call attempt, yet most leads get one or two. Let the CRM schedule the attempts so persistence doesn't depend on memory. Copy a follow-up cadence .
3. Treat a missed call as a lead, not a voicemail
Only 2% of unanswered callers leave a voicemail. Turn every missed call into a callback task and a text within minutes. See what yours cost with the missed call calculator .
4. Fix the data before buying more leads
76% of CRM users say less than half their data is accurate. Required lead source, next follow-up date and dead reason fix most of it. Use the CRM field kit .
5. Margins are thinner, so every lead counts
Flip ROI fell to 25.5% in 2025, the lowest since 2008, and investor purchases are down. Teams that keep more of the leads they already pay for will outlast teams that just buy more.
How these were checked
Every statistic was read on the linked page in October 2026. Where the original was paywalled or blocked (the HBR article and the Velocify study), I used a contemporaneous report of it and say so. Vendor research (InsideSales, Velocify, Invoca, CallRail, Validity, HubSpot, Carrot, BatchData) is labeled by publisher so you can weigh it. Most lead-response research is not specific to real estate. Spotted an error or a newer source? Email a correction .

## Rental Yield & Cap Rate Calculator (USD, CAD, GBP, EUR)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/rental-yield-calculator.html

Rental yield & cap rate calculator.
Gross yield, net yield, cap rate and cash-on-cash return for any rental or buy-to-let property. Include purchase costs such as closing costs, stamp duty or transfer tax as one figure. Built for real estate investors in the United States, Canada, the UK and Europe. Pick your currency; the math is the same everywhere.
The formula
Gross yield = annual rent ÷ purchase price
Net operating income (NOI) = annual rent × (1 − vacancy) − running costs
Net yield = NOI ÷ (price + purchase costs + renovation)
Cap rate = NOI ÷ purchase price
Cash-on-cash = (NOI − annual mortgage payments) ÷ cash invested
Worked example
A $250,000 property with $10,000 of purchase costs rents for $1,750 a month. Gross yield is 8.40%. Allow 5% for vacancy and $4,500 a year of running costs and the net operating income is $15,450, a 5.94% net yield and a 6.18% cap rate. With a $187,500 repayment mortgage at 5.5% over 25 years ($13,817 a year), cash flow is $1,633 a year on $72,500 invested.
Questions
What is the difference between gross and net rental yield?
Gross yield is the annual rent divided by the purchase price, before any costs. Net yield subtracts running costs and vacancy, and divides by everything you paid including purchase costs and renovation. Net yield is the one to compare properties with.
Is cap rate the same as net yield?
Close, but not the same. Cap rate is net operating income divided by the purchase price only. Net yield in this calculator divides by price plus purchase costs and renovation, so it is usually a little lower. US investors tend to quote cap rate; UK and European investors tend to quote yield.
What is a good rental yield?
There is no single number. Yields depend on the country, city, property type and interest rates. Compare a property against similar rentals in the same area, and check that the cash flow is positive after the mortgage.
Should I include stamp duty or transfer tax?
Yes, in purchase costs. Stamp duty in the UK, land transfer tax in Canada, transfer tax in the US and registration or transfer taxes across Europe all add to what you paid, so they lower your net yield. Rates and surcharges for additional properties vary; check the current rules where you buy.
How do I track yield across a portfolio?
Store rent, running costs, purchase costs and loan terms as fields on each property record in your CRM, with yield and cash flow as formulas. A portfolio report then ranks properties by net yield every month.

BRRRR calculator · DSCR calculator · Cost per deal by lead source · All free tools
Last updated October 2026. For planning only, not financial, tax or legal advice. Check figures with your lender, accountant or lawyer.

## Salesforce AI & Agentforce for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-ai-agentforce-real-estate.html

Salesforce AI and Agentforce for real estate investors.
Salesforce’s 2026 AI for sales is Agentforce, plus Einstein features like Conversation Insights and Lead Scoring. For real estate investors, the useful parts today are call analysis and activity capture on data you already have; agents that write to sellers need consent rules first. Here’s what each feature does, where it’s available and how to get your CRM ready.
Salesforce’s 2026 sales AI is Agentforce : agents for prospecting, lead engagement, pipeline management and coaching. They consume usage-based credits, and Salesforce says to confirm licensing with your account team. source
For investors, the most practical AI is not an agent writing to sellers. It’s call analysis (Einstein Conversation Insights) and activity capture , which work on data you already have. source · EAC
AI on top of messy data repeats the mess. Fix lead source, call outcomes and stages first.
What AI does Salesforce Sales Cloud offer in 2026?
Feature | What it does | Availability (per Salesforce Help)
Agentforce Prospecting | Builds a prioritized list of contacts and accounts for reps | Usage-based credits; confirm with account team
Agentforce Engagement (formerly Lead Nurturing) | Web chat to leads and email nurturing via Outlook or Gmail | Enterprise, Performance or Unlimited with Sales and Einstein for Sales
Agentforce Sales Management | Pipeline and account management assistance | Usage-based credits
Agentforce Sales Coach | Real-time feedback and role-play | Usage-based credits
Einstein Conversation Insights | Analyzes recorded calls for keywords, mentions and next steps; connectors include RingCentral, Dialpad and Aircall | Starter, Pro, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, Agentforce 1 Sales
Einstein Lead Scoring | Scores leads from your past conversions, refreshed every 10 days | Needs Sales Cloud Einstein
Einstein Activity Capture | Syncs email and calendar activity to Salesforce | Standard in Starter through Enterprise
Sources: Sales Cloud agents · Agentforce Engagement · Conversation Insights · Lead Scoring · Activity Capture . In June 2025, Agentforce 1 editions replaced Einstein 1 editions. source
Which AI uses actually help a wholesaling team?
Call review at scale
Conversation Insights can flag calls where sellers mention keywords you choose, like foreclosure, probate, divorce or a deadline. A manager reviews the flagged calls instead of random ones.
Lead scoring, once you have history
Einstein Lead Scoring learns from your past converted leads. A team with few closed deals gets a weak model; Salesforce uses a global model when you lack data. source
Summaries for the handoff
Summaries of long seller conversations help acquisitions pick up where the caller left off. The structured fields (timeline, reason, condition) still matter more; see the handoff checklist .
Careful with agents that write to sellers
An agent emailing or texting sellers is still marketing outreach. Consent, opt-outs and tone apply, and CTIA’s guidance calls for express written consent for marketing texts. source See the texting guide .
Is your CRM ready for AI?
Check | Why
Lead source is a picklist, set automatically | Scoring and attribution learn from it
Calls are recorded and logged to the lead | Conversation analysis needs the recordings on the record
Stages have entry rules | Otherwise the model learns from inconsistent stages
Dead reasons are required | So the model can tell bad leads from bad follow-up
Enough closed deals | Scoring from your own history needs history
Score your setup in two minutes with the Deal Leak Score . More: Salesforce AI for real estate .
Questions
What is Agentforce in Salesforce?
Agentforce is Salesforce’s family of AI agents. In Sales Cloud they include Prospecting, Engagement (lead nurturing), Sales Management and Sales Coach, billed with usage-based credits.
Can Salesforce AI analyze my acquisition calls?
Einstein Conversation Insights analyzes recorded calls for keywords and next steps, with voice connectors including RingCentral, Dialpad and Aircall.
Should an AI agent text or email my sellers?
Only with consent and opt-outs in place. Marketing messages to sellers are still marketing, and CTIA’s guidance calls for express written consent for marketing texts.
Do I need clean data before using Salesforce AI?
Yes. Scoring and analysis learn from your fields; free-text lead sources, unlogged calls and inconsistent stages produce unreliable results.

## 15 Salesforce Automations for Wholesalers (Recipes)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-automation-recipes-wholesalers.html

15 automation recipes for a wholesaling CRM.
The automations that pay off first in a wholesaling CRM are a call task for every new lead, a callback for every missed call, required fields before a lead is passed, and long follow-up for “not now” leads. Here are 15 recipes written as trigger → action, which Salesforce tool to use for each, and the order to build them.
These are the automations I’d build first for a wholesaling team, written as trigger → action so you can hand them to whoever builds your CRM.
Count them before you pick an edition: Salesforce Professional allows 5 flows; Enterprise allows 2,000 active. source · source
Several are better as validation rules, approval processes or dashboard subscriptions than as flows.
15 automations for a wholesaling CRM
Automation | Trigger | Action | Fixes | Salesforce tool
New lead → owner and call task | Lead created | Assign by market or round robin; create call task due in 5 minutes; alert owner | Speed to lead | Record-triggered
Missed inbound call → callback | Call logged with outcome = missed, direction = inbound | Task due in 10 minutes for lead owner; if consented, send text | Missed calls | Record-triggered on Task
No activity in 7 days | Daily at 7am: open leads with last activity > 7 days | Follow-up task for owner; after 3 sweeps, flag for manager | Follow-up | Schedule-triggered
“Not now” → re-contact date | Status changes to Not now | Require re-contact date; create task on that date; enroll in long cadence | Long follow-up | Record-triggered
Warm/hot handoff check | Status changes to Warm or Hot | Block save without timeline, reason, condition, callback time (validation rule); task for acquisitions due same day / within 1 hour | Handoff | Validation rule + record-triggered
Offer above MAO → approval | Offer amount > MAO on the deal | Route to acquisitions manager for approval before status can be Sent | Offer discipline | Flow Approval Process
Offer expires | Daily: offers sent > 5 days with no response | Task to follow up; mark expired after 14 days | Offers | Schedule-triggered
Signed contract → under contract | Signed document written back by e-signature tool | Stage = Under contract; task for TC; post to #dispo | Contract to dispo | Record-triggered
Under contract → buyer match | Stage = Under contract | Create Deal Sent records for top 10 matching buyers; task for dispo | Dispo speed | Record-triggered
Closing date in 3 days | Daily: deals closing in 3 days | Checklist task for TC (title, funds, buyer confirmation) | Closing | Schedule-triggered
Deal dies → reason and source kept | Stage = Dead | Require dead reason; if “not now”, create re-contact date | Clean ROI | Validation rule + record-triggered
Fall-out → out of ROI | Contract cancelled | Uncheck “counts in ROI”; notify owner; reopen lead with reason | Honest reporting | Record-triggered
Duplicate seller → merge task | Duplicate rule alert on new lead | Task to merge; keep first lead source | Data quality | Duplicate rule + task
Proof of funds stale | Daily: buyers with POF date > 90 days | Task to request a new POF | Dispo | Schedule-triggered
Monday numbers | Monday 7am | Dashboard emailed to owner and managers | Weekly review | Dashboard subscription
Flow, validation rule or approval: which tool for which job?
Job | Tool | Why
Stop bad data being saved | Validation rule | Enforced everywhere, including imports and integrations
React to a change | Record-triggered flow | Runs when a record is created, updated or deleted
Sweep records on a timetable | Schedule-triggered flow | Runs at set times on batches of records
Guide a rep through a script | Screen flow | Shows only the questions that apply
Manager sign-off | Flow Approval Process | Multistep approvals with work items; Enterprise and up
Sources: Flow types · Flow Approval Processes .
Which automations should you build first?
Week 1
New lead task, missed call callback, warm/hot validation. These protect the leads you already pay for. See speed to lead and the handoff checklist .
Week 2
No activity sweep, not-now re-contact, dead reason. These protect the long follow-up where most conversions happen .
Week 3
Contract to dispo, buyer match, closing checklist. These shorten days to assignment.
Week 4
Offer approvals, fall-outs out of ROI, Monday dashboard. These make the numbers honest.
What goes wrong with CRM automation?
Building automations before the fields are clean: a flow that reads a free-text lead source does nothing useful.
Too many alerts: if every change pings someone, people mute them. Alert on exceptions only.
No owner: every automation should have a person who gets told when it fails.
Overlapping tools: a Zapier chain and a flow both creating tasks doubles the work. See replacing Zapier chains .
Questions
What should a wholesaler automate first in a CRM?
The new-lead call task, a callback task for missed calls, and required fields before a lead is marked warm or hot. They protect leads you already paid for.
How many flows can Salesforce Professional run?
Salesforce’s Professional Edition allocation page lists 5 flows. Enterprise and Unlimited allow 4,000 total and 2,000 active.
Should required fields be a flow or a validation rule?
A validation rule. It blocks the save everywhere, including imports and integrations, and can be conditional on stage or status.
Sources
Salesforce Help: Flow types
Salesforce Help: Professional Edition allocations
Salesforce Help: Enterprise Edition allocations
Salesforce Help: Flow Approval Processes

## Salesforce Dialers for Real Estate: Open CTI Ends 2028
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-dialer-real-estate.html

Dialers in Salesforce for real estate teams.
RingCentral, Aircall, Dialpad and Twilio all log calls into Salesforce, but Salesforce’s Open CTI, which many of them use, reaches end of life on February 28, 2028. Here’s how each dialer connects, which edition it needs, what a wholesaling team should log, and how to plan for 2028.
Salesforce says Open CTI reaches end of life on February 28, 2028, and existing implementations stop working after that. Salesforce Voice is the recommended replacement. source
Many dialer integrations use Open CTI; Twilio Flex’s docs say its Salesforce integration will stop working after that date. source
Edition matters: RingCentral supports Professional and above; Aircall and Dialpad require Enterprise or Unlimited. RingCentral · Aircall · Dialpad
The last two numbers are from my speed to lead statistics page , with sources.
How do the main dialers connect to Salesforce?
Dialer | What it does in Salesforce | Salesforce edition | Other requirements
RingCentral for Salesforce | Click to dial and click to text, automatic call and message logging, screen pops, voicemail, in-app calling | Professional and above | RingCentral Advanced or Ultra; admin install
Aircall | Calls in and out from Salesforce; logs details, tags and recordings; works across leads, contacts and accounts | Enterprise or Unlimited | Aircall Professional plan; same email in both systems
Dialpad | CTI, power dialer, call logging; SMS logged as completed tasks on the contact (not opportunities) | Enterprise or Unlimited, API enabled | Dialpad Connect, Support or Sell license
Twilio Flex | Agent UI inside Salesforce; click to dial, screen pop, activity logging | Not stated | Flex account; subject to the Open CTI retirement
Salesforce Voice | Native telephony with Amazon Connect; Salesforce’s recommended Open CTI replacement | Licensed separately | —
Sources: RingCentral · RingCentral FAQ · Aircall · Dialpad · Dialpad SMS logging · Twilio Flex · Salesforce Voice
What does the Open CTI retirement mean for an investor?
If your dialer runs inside Salesforce today, ask the vendor whether it uses Open CTI. Nothing breaks before February 28, 2028, but anything you build now should have a path past it. Dialpad, for example, says Dialpad for Salesforce is not being retired and lists Salesforce Voice or Dialpad Everywhere as options. source
Ask your dialer vendor, in writing, what their post-2028 Salesforce integration is.
Keep call outcomes in your own Salesforce fields, not only in the vendor’s objects, so reports survive a switch.
If you’re choosing a dialer now, weigh the vendor’s 2028 plan as much as today’s features.
What should a dialer integration log for a wholesaling team?
Field | Why
Call outcome (picklist) | Contact rate and conversion by list; see the handoff checklist
Call direction and duration | Separates inbound sellers from outbound dials
Recording link | Coaching and dispute checks
Missed inbound call → task | Only 2% of unanswered callers leave a voicemail; the task is the callback. See the missed call calculator
Attempt number | Follow-up cadence reporting; the median web lead got one contact attempt (InsideSales, 2014)
Recorded calls can also feed Einstein Conversation Insights, which lists RingCentral, Dialpad and Aircall among its voice connectors. source
Questions
Is Salesforce Open CTI being retired?
Yes. Salesforce Help says Open CTI reaches end of life on February 28, 2028, existing implementations stop working after that, and Salesforce Voice is the recommended replacement.
Which dialer works with Salesforce Professional Edition?
RingCentral lists Professional and above. Aircall and Dialpad require Enterprise or Unlimited.
Can Salesforce log texts from my dialer?
Some dialers do. Dialpad logs SMS as completed tasks on the contact’s activity history, but not on opportunities and not from shared lines. RingCentral logs calls and messages.
What is the best dialer for wholesalers using Salesforce?
It depends on your edition and volume. Check the Salesforce edition each vendor requires, how calls are logged, and the vendor’s plan after Open CTI ends in 2028.

## Wholesale Dispositions in Salesforce: Buyers & Deals
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-dispositions-real-estate.html

Wholesale dispositions in Salesforce.
A dispo system in Salesforce has three parts: buyer records with a structured buy box, a record of every deal sent to every buyer, and a fast way to send new contracts to the best-matched buyers first. Here’s the data model, matching rules, sending options, automations and the numbers that show whether your buyer list is real.
Dispo in a CRM means three things: buyers with a buy box , a record of which buyers saw which deal , and a fast way to send a new deal to the right buyers first .
In Salesforce that’s a Buyer record, a junction object between Property and Buyer, and List Email or an email tool. List Email sends to up to 200 leads or contacts at once. source
The payoff: when a contract is signed, the 10 buyers most likely to close get it in minutes, and you can see who actually buys.
What records does a dispo system need?
Record | Key fields | Why
Buyer (Contact or custom object) | Zips or counties, min/max price, property types, rehab level, financing (cash or hard money), proof of funds date, last purchase date | Matching a deal to the buy box
Property / Deal | Address, ARV, repairs, contract price, assignment ask, access instructions, photos folder | What you’re selling
Deal Sent (junction: Property ↔ Buyer) | Date sent, opened or viewed, interested, offer amount, outcome | Who saw what, who offered, who closes
The junction record is the part most teams skip. In Salesforce it’s two master-detail relationships, and it can roll up to both sides: offers per deal and deals sent per buyer. source · roll-up limits
How do you match a deal to the right buyers?
Start with the buy box
A list view or report filtered by the deal’s zip, price band and property type gives the candidate buyers. Keep the buy box as picklists and numbers, not a notes field, or the filter can’t work.
Rank by behaviour, not list size
Sort candidates by deals closed in the last 12 months, then by offers made. A roll-up on the buyer record makes this one column.
Send to the top 10 first
Give your best buyers a head start, then widen. The Deal Sent records show who had the chance, which settles “I never got that one.”
How do you send deals to buyers from Salesforce?
Option | Good for | Limit or note
List Email | Up to 200 buyers at a time from a list view | Counts toward the mass email limit, typically 5,000 recipients a day
Mailchimp (Beaufort 12 integration) | Designed deal emails to segmented buyer audiences | Third-party integration; email activity shows on Salesforce records
Account Engagement | Larger lists, scoring and automation | Syncs with Professional and higher every 2–4 minutes
Text | Buyers who agreed to texts | See the texting and 10DLC guide
Sources: List Email · Mailchimp · Account Engagement
Should buyers get a portal?
A buyer portal lets buyers log in and see available deals, request access and submit offers. In Salesforce that’s Experience Cloud, which needs Enterprise or higher and licenses bought separately. For most wholesalers, a good email and a deal page per property is enough until volume justifies it. source
What should dispo automate?
Under contract → post to the #dispo Slack channel with address, ARV and assignment ask. Flow has a Send Message to Slack action. source
Under contract → create the deal folder (Box for Salesforce puts a folder on each record). source
Buyer offer received → task for the dispo rep and update the Deal Sent record.
No buyer interest in 72 hours → task to re-price or widen the list.
Proof of funds older than 90 days → task to request a new one.
Which dispo numbers matter?
Number | Tells you
Days from contract to assignment | Whether your buyer list is deep enough
Buyers who closed in the last 12 months | Your real buyer list (often a small fraction of the total)
Offers per deal sent | Pricing and deal quality
Assignment fee vs ask | How much you give up to close
Fall-outs by buyer | Who to stop sending deals to first
A Kanban view of the dispo pipeline, summarized by expected fee, gives the team a daily board. source Free template: cash buyers list .
Questions
How do wholesalers track cash buyers in a CRM?
Store each buyer with a structured buy box (areas, price range, property types, rehab level, financing, proof of funds date) and log every deal sent to them, so you can filter matching buyers and see who actually buys.
Can Salesforce send a new deal to my buyers list?
Yes. List Email sends a template to up to 200 contacts or leads at a time from a list view. For larger lists or designed emails, use an email tool connected to Salesforce.
Do I need a buyer portal?
Usually not at first. Salesforce portals use Experience Cloud, which needs Enterprise or higher and separate licenses. Email plus a deal page works for most wholesalers.
What is a buy box?
A buyer’s criteria for deals: locations, price range, property types, condition and how they fund purchases.

## DocuSign + Salesforce for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-docusign-real-estate.html

DocuSign + Salesforce for real estate investors.
DocuSign connects to Salesforce through Docusign’s own AppExchange package : you send purchase and assignment contracts from the deal record, templates fill themselves from Salesforce fields, and signed documents come back to the record. Here’s what it does, what it needs and how I set it up for wholesalers.
Docusign builds Docusign eSignature for Salesforce , an AppExchange package that sends agreements from Salesforce records and writes signed documents and signer data back. source
Templates pull record fields through merge fields, so seller name, property address and price fill themselves. source
Salesforce lists it as working with Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Starter and Performance. It needs a separate Docusign subscription. source
What does DocuSign do inside Salesforce?
Capability | What Docusign’s listing says | What I use it for in wholesaling
Send from a record | Send agreements to Salesforce contacts or any email, with messages, reminders and authentication | Purchase agreement to the seller from the deal, not from someone’s inbox
Templates with merge fields | “Create agreements from Docusign templates that use Salesforce data through merge fields” | Seller name, address, price and closing date typed once in Salesforce, never retyped in a PDF
Write-back | “Signed documents and signer-provided data are written back to Salesforce” | The signed contract lives on the deal; title, dispo and the owner all see the same file
Mobile | Mobile-responsive signing and Salesforce mobile support | Sellers sign on a phone at the kitchen table
Setup | “Clicks-not-code”; the package’s tabs and objects don’t count against org limits | No custom code needed for the basic flow
Sources: AppExchange listing · Salesforce integration page . Docusign also sells Gen for Salesforce (documents generated from Salesforce data) and CLM for Salesforce (contract templates and workflows). source
What does a contract flow look like for a wholesaler?
1. Offer accepted
The acquisitions rep clicks Send with Docusign on the deal. The purchase agreement template fills from the deal: seller, address, price, earnest money, closing date.
2. Seller signs
The signed PDF and signer data come back to the deal. I key a Flow on that write-back to move the stage to Under Contract and create the title-company task.
3. Dispo assigns
The assignment contract template goes to the end buyer from the same deal, with the assignment price and fee filled in.
4. Everything in one place
Both signed contracts sit on the deal. When a closing gets delayed or a buyer backs out, nobody has to search email for “the latest version”.
Before you build this, make sure the fields exist: contract price, assignment price, assignment fee , closing date, title company. Those are what the templates merge.
What should you check before installing?
A Docusign plan with the Salesforce integration. The AppExchange listing shows a published price of “starts at $30 per user per month” and a 30-day free trial (as of October 2026). source
Your contract templates reviewed by your attorney for each state you buy in. The integration fills fields; it doesn’t make a contract valid.
Which record you send from. I send from the deal (Opportunity or a custom Deal object), not the lead, so every contract stays with the property.
Docusign’s status-object details. I couldn’t read Docusign’s admin guide pages (they only load with JavaScript), so confirm the exact objects in the admin guide before building reports on them.
Questions
Can I send a purchase agreement from Salesforce with DocuSign?
Yes. With Docusign eSignature for Salesforce installed, you send agreements from a record using a Docusign template whose merge fields pull data from Salesforce, and the signed document is written back to Salesforce.
Does DocuSign for Salesforce work on Professional Edition?
Salesforce lists Docusign as working with Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Starter and Performance editions.
Can a signed DocuSign contract update the deal stage?
The package writes signed documents and signer data back to Salesforce. A record-triggered Flow can react to that write-back and move the stage. Confirm which object changes in Docusign’s admin guide before you build it.
Do I need a separate DocuSign subscription?
Yes. The integration requires a Docusign plan; the AppExchange listing shows pricing and a 30-day free trial.

## Which Salesforce Edition Do Real Estate Investors Need?
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-edition-real-estate-investors.html

Which Salesforce edition do real estate investors need?
Most real estate investing teams need Salesforce Enterprise , because it allows 200 custom objects for properties, offers and buyers, 2,000 active flows and API access for integrations. Professional can work for small teams that fit in 5 flows; Starter can’t hold property records at all. Here’s the comparison, from Salesforce’s own limits pages.
Starter allows 0 custom objects, so it can’t hold Property, Offer or Buyer records. Fine for a solo investor tracking contacts; not a wholesaling system. source
Professional / Pro Suite allows 50 custom objects but only 5 flows, and API access is an add-on for Professional (and shown as an add-on for Pro Suite on Salesforce’s pricing page), which many integrations need. source · source
Enterprise is where most growing investor teams land: 200 custom objects, 2,000 active flows, API included, approvals and joined reports. source
Don’t compare on list price. Most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive based on the business and number of users.
What can each Salesforce edition do for an investor?
 | Starter | Professional / Pro Suite | Enterprise | Unlimited
Custom objects (Property, Offer, Buyer) | 0 | 50 | 200 | 2,000
Custom fields per object | 25 | 100 | 500 | 800
Flows | Not listed | 5 | 4,000 (2,000 active) | 4,000 (2,000 active)
Active validation rules per object | 20 | 20 | 100 | 500
API access (needed by many integrations) | Not stated | Add-on | Included | Included
Flow Approval Processes | — | — | Yes | Yes
Joined reports | — | — | Yes | Yes
Custom report types | — | 50 | 300 | 2,000
Sales Engagement cadences | — | Extra cost | Extra cost | Included
Experience Cloud portals | — | — | Yes, licenses extra | Yes, licenses extra
Data Loader | — | Via API add-on | Yes | Yes
Sources: Starter · Pro Suite · Professional · Enterprise · Unlimited · API · API by edition · approvals · reports · Sales Engagement · Experience Cloud · import tools . Pro Suite and Professional allocations match on the pages read.
Which edition fits which investor?
Solo investor, a few deals a year
You may not need Salesforce at all. If you do, the question is whether you need Property and Offer records; if yes, Starter won’t do it. See do I need a CRM yet? and when Salesforce is overkill .
Small team, one market, few integrations
Professional or Pro Suite can work if 5 flows cover your automation and your phone and e-signature tools support it (DocuSign and RingCentral list Professional). Count your flows before you buy.
Team with acquisitions, dispo and VAs, several lead sources
Enterprise. You’ll want more than 5 flows within months, approvals for offers above MAO, joined reports, and API access for CallRail, Google Ads conversion import, Calendly or Aircall, which require it or Enterprise outright. CallRail · Calendly
Multiple markets or a fund with investor reporting
Enterprise or Unlimited, depending on volume, sandbox needs and whether Sales Engagement cadences are worth having included.
Why do Salesforce edition names keep changing?
Salesforce repackages often. In June 2025, Agentforce 1 editions replaced Einstein 1 editions. source Third-party reports say Salesforce introduced Core, Advanced and Max editions in September 2026, with existing customers keeping their edition; I couldn’t read Salesforce’s own announcement. Either way, map your needs to the limits above (custom objects, flows, API access) and ask your account executive which current edition delivers them.
Not sure? Answer nine questions in the free edition picker .
What does Salesforce cost for an investor?
I don’t publish list prices, because most businesses don’t pay them. After a conversation with a Salesforce account executive, many get a discount based on the business and the number of users. Get a quote for your exact user count and edition, then add the setup cost, before you compare with an investor CRM.
Questions
Which Salesforce edition is best for wholesalers?
Most wholesaling teams with several roles and lead sources fit Enterprise: 200 custom objects, 2,000 active flows and API access included. Professional can work for small teams if 5 flows and its integrations are enough.
Can Salesforce Starter track properties?
Not as separate records. Starter allows 0 custom objects, so you can’t add Property, Offer or Buyer objects.
Does Salesforce Professional include API access?
No. Salesforce says Professional can add API access as an add-on; it’s included by default in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer.
How many flows does Professional Edition allow?
Salesforce’s allocation page for Professional lists 5 flows, versus 4,000 total and 2,000 active in Enterprise and Unlimited.
Do investors pay Salesforce list price?
Most businesses don’t. A Salesforce account executive can offer a discount based on the business and number of users, so get a quote before comparing.

## Salesforce Features for Real Estate Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-features-real-estate.html

Salesforce features that matter for real estate investors.
For real estate investors, the Salesforce features that pay off are custom objects, Flow automation, validation rules, lead routing and reporting : they turn a contact list into a system that tracks every property, offer and buyer. Below are 37 features, what each does for a wholesaling or investing team, and the edition limits that decide whether you can use it.
The Salesforce features that matter most to investors aren’t the AI headlines. They’re custom objects (Property, Offer, Buyer), Flow automation, validation rules , assignment rules and reports .
Starter allows 0 custom objects , so it can’t hold a Property or Offer object. Professional allows 50 and only 5 flows; Enterprise allows 200 objects and 2,000 active flows. source · source · source
Each feature below has what it does, how a wholesaling or investing team uses it, and the edition or limit to know, linked to Salesforce’s own documentation.
Jump to: Data model Automation Routing Data quality Reporting Outreach Mobile Portals AI Security Import By edition
Can Salesforce model properties, offers and buyers?
Yes, with custom objects and relationships. This is the biggest difference from most investor CRMs, which give you a fixed lead-and-deal structure.
Custom objects
What it does: Your own record types with their own fields, layouts and reports. In real estate: A Property object (one record per address, however many times it’s marketed), an Offer object (every offer, not just the last one), a Buyer object with buy box fields. Edition / limit: Starter 0, Pro Suite and Professional 50, Enterprise 200, Unlimited 2,000. Custom fields per object: 25 / 100 / 100 / 500 / 800. source
Lookup and master-detail relationships
What it does: Link records. Master-detail deletes children with the parent and allows roll-ups; lookup doesn’t. In real estate: Offers as master-detail children of a Property, so “number of offers” and “highest offer” roll up. Seller as a lookup, because one seller can own several properties. Edition / limit: 2 master-detail and 40 total relationships per object. source
Junction objects
What it does: A many-to-many link built from two master-detail relationships. In real estate: Property ↔ Buyer: which buyers were sent which deal, who viewed it, who offered. That’s your dispo history. Edition / limit: Can carry roll-ups to both parents. source
Roll-up summary fields
What it does: Count, sum, min or max of child records on the parent. In real estate: Offers per property, total assignment fees per lead source, deals per buyer. Edition / limit: 25 per object by default, up to 40 via Support. source
Formula fields
What it does: Read-only fields calculated from other fields. In real estate: MAO = ARV × 70% − repairs. Assignment fee = buyer price − contract price. Days since last contact. Edition / limit: All editions; up to 3,900 characters. source · see the MAO calculator
What can Salesforce automate for a real estate team?
Flow (record-triggered)
What it does: Runs when a record is created, updated or deleted. In real estate: New lead → task for the assigned rep due in 5 minutes. Missed call → callback task. Stage = Under Contract → post to the dispo channel. Edition / limit: Professional and Pro Suite: 5 flows. Enterprise and Unlimited: 4,000 total, 2,000 active. source · Professional · Enterprise
Flow (schedule-triggered)
What it does: Runs at a set time and frequency on a batch of records. In real estate: Every morning: leads with no activity in 7 days get a follow-up task. Every Monday: stale offers flagged. Edition / limit: Same flow allocation as above. source
Screen flows
What it does: Guided forms with steps and logic. In real estate: A seller intake script that asks timeline, condition and reason, and only shows the asking-price question when the lead is hot. See the cold caller handoff checklist . Edition / limit: Same flow allocation. source
Flow Approval Processes
What it does: Multistep approvals where each step assigns a work item to a user, group or queue. In real estate: Offers above MAO, or above a dollar threshold, need the acquisitions manager’s approval before they go out. Edition / limit: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer; Lightning only. Salesforce calls it the modern alternative to classic approval processes. source · editions
More examples: 15 automation recipes for wholesalers · 5 Salesforce automations every real estate team needs .
How does Salesforce assign leads to the right rep?
Lead assignment rules
What it does: Ordered rule entries; the first match assigns the lead to a user or queue. In real estate: Leads from a market or zip code go to that market’s acquisitions rep; PPC leads go to the senior closer. Edition / limit: Up to 25 criteria per entry. source
Round robin
What it does: Salesforce’s documented method uses an autonumber field, a MOD formula and one assignment entry per rep. In real estate: Even split of inbound leads across 3 reps. Change the divisor when a rep joins or leaves. Edition / limit: Method from Salesforce Help. source
Queues
What it does: Shared buckets that team members claim records from. In real estate: A “Hot seller callbacks” queue anyone on the team can claim from when the owner is on another call. Edition / limit: No limit on the number of queues. source
Full setup: Salesforce lead and call routing for real estate teams .
How do you keep CRM data clean?
Validation rules
What it does: Block a save when the data breaks a rule you define, with your error message. In real estate: A warm or hot lead can’t be saved without timeline, reason and condition. A deal can’t move to Under Contract without a contract price. Edition / limit: Active rules per object: Professional 20, Enterprise 100, Unlimited 500. source · allocations
Four ways to require a field
What it does: Field-level (enforced everywhere, including imports), page layout (screen only), validation rule (conditional, everywhere), Dynamic Forms (that page only). In real estate: Use a validation rule for “required at this stage”. Use field-level only for fields every record has from day one, or imports will fail. Edition / limit: Salesforce Help comparison. source
Dynamic Forms
What it does: Show or hide fields based on record data, user or device. In real estate: Show the assignment fields only when exit type = assignment; show double close costs only for double closes. Edition / limit: Group, Essentials, Professional and up. source
Duplicate and matching rules
What it does: Block or alert when a new record matches an existing one. In real estate: The same seller arrives from a mailer, a web form and a list import. Match on phone and property address. Edition / limit: Up to 5 active duplicate rules per object. source
Path
What it does: A stage bar with key fields and guidance per stage. In real estate: Lead → Appointment → Offer → Under Contract → Assigned / Closed, with what the rep must capture at each step. Edition / limit: Up to 5 key fields and 1,000 characters of guidance per step. source
Kanban view
What it does: Drag-and-drop board of a list view, grouped and totaled. In real estate: Dispo pipeline by stage, summarized by expected assignment fee. Edition / limit: Essentials, Group, Professional and up; Lightning only. source
Field history tracking
What it does: Records old value, new value, who and when. In real estate: See who changed the lead source or the stage, and when. (Currency fields aren’t supported, so price changes need another approach.) Edition / limit: 20 fields per object; 18 months in the UI and 24 via the API without Field Audit Trail. source · retention
What reports can Salesforce build for investors?
Custom report types
What it does: Define which objects and fields a report can use. In real estate: Lead source → deal → assignment fee in one report, which is how you get cost per deal by source . Edition / limit: Professional 50, Enterprise 300, Unlimited 2,000. source
Joined reports and cross filters
What it does: Several report blocks side by side; filters like “leads without activities”. In real estate: Leads with no call in 7 days. Offers made vs contracts signed by rep, side by side. Edition / limit: Joined reports: Enterprise and up, 5 blocks. Cross filters: 3 per report. source
Reporting snapshots
What it does: Save report results to a custom object on a schedule. In real estate: Pipeline value every Monday, so you can chart the trend, not just today’s number. Pairs with the Monday 5 KPIs . Edition / limit: Professional and up; Professional allows 200. source
Dashboard subscriptions
What it does: Dashboards emailed on a schedule. In real estate: The owner gets the weekly numbers in their inbox without logging in. Edition / limit: Up to 500 recipients per subscription. source
Examples: 20 report recipes · pipeline dashboard · real estate KPIs in Salesforce .
Can Salesforce handle follow-up and email?
Web-to-Lead and auto-response rules
What it does: A website form creates a lead; an automatic email replies. In real estate: The “sell your house” form creates a lead with its campaign, and the seller gets a confirmation instantly. Edition / limit: 500 leads per 24 hours; one active lead auto-response rule. source · auto-response
List Email
What it does: Send a template to up to 200 leads or contacts at once. In real estate: A new-deal email to buyers in one zip code. Edition / limit: Counts toward the mass email limit, typically 5,000 recipients a day. source
Sales Engagement cadences
What it does: Sequences of calls, emails and tasks that appear in a rep’s work queue. In real estate: A seller follow-up cadence that runs for months, not days. Edition / limit: Included in Unlimited; extra cost in Professional and Enterprise. source
Einstein Activity Capture
What it does: Syncs email and calendar activity from Gmail or Microsoft to Salesforce. In real estate: Every email with a title company or buyer shows on the record. Edition / limit: Standard version in Starter through Enterprise; 6 months of activity stored. source
Does the Salesforce mobile app work in the field?
Offline and Offline Edit
What it does: Caches recent records and lets users create and edit offline; changes sync later. In real estate: Walkthrough notes in a basement with no signal; driving for dollars in rural areas. Edition / limit: Caches 30 recent records for each of 5 recent objects by default. source
Business card scan
What it does: Create contacts by scanning a card. In real estate: Meeting buyers and agents at a REIA meetup. Edition / limit: All editions except Database.com. source
Field workflow: driving for dollars with Salesforce .
Can buyers or partners log in?
Experience Cloud
What it does: External sites with Salesforce data and logins. In real estate: A cash buyer portal that shows available deals; a JV or bird-dog portal for submitting leads. Edition / limit: Enterprise and up; licenses bought separately. Partner Community is the license for lead and opportunity portals. source
Buyer side: wholesale dispositions in Salesforce .
What AI does Salesforce offer in 2026?
Agentforce sales agents
What it does: Agents for prospecting, lead engagement, pipeline management and coaching. In real estate: Agentforce Engagement can email-nurture cold seller leads; check consent and tone before you let anything write to sellers. Edition / limit: Usage-based credits; Agentforce Engagement needs Enterprise, Performance or Unlimited with Sales and Einstein for Sales. source
Einstein Conversation Insights
What it does: Analyzes recorded calls for keywords, mentions and next steps. In real estate: Flag calls where sellers mention foreclosure, probate or a deadline. Edition / limit: Listed for Starter, Pro, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Agentforce 1 Sales; connectors include RingCentral, Dialpad and Aircall. source
More: Salesforce AI and Agentforce for investors · Salesforce AI for real estate .
How do you control who sees what?
Permission sets
What it does: Add permissions on top of a profile; Salesforce’s recommended approach. In real estate: VAs can create leads but not see deal financials; dispo sees buyers but not seller notes. Edition / limit: All main editions. source
Sharing rules and field-level security
What it does: Open record access beyond defaults; hide specific fields. In real estate: Market teams see their own market; only owners see assignment fee fields. Edition / limit: Sharing rules: Professional and up, 300 per object. FLS: Professional and up. source · FLS
Multi-factor authentication
What it does: Required for all employee logins. In real estate: Matters when VAs log in from other countries. Plan it into onboarding. Edition / limit: Production enforcement rolled out July 20 to September 3, 2026. source
Role-by-role setup: Salesforce access for VAs and cold callers .
How do you get lists into Salesforce?
Data Import Wizard
What it does: Browser-based import for leads, contacts, accounts and custom objects. In real estate: A county list or a skip-traced list from PropStream. Edition / limit: Up to 50,000 records at a time; all editions except Personal and Database.com. source · tool comparison
Data Loader
What it does: Desktop tool for large imports, updates and exports. In real estate: Lists over 50,000 rows, or a full migration from Podio or another CRM. Edition / limit: Enterprise and up by default; uses the API, which is an add-on for Professional. source · API editions
Moving from another CRM: Salesforce CRM migration for real estate · moving off Podio .

Most businesses don’t pay list price: a Salesforce account executive can discount based on your business and number of users, so get a quote before comparing. Questions
What Salesforce features are most useful for real estate investors?
Custom objects for properties, offers and buyers; Flow for follow-up and missed-call tasks; validation rules so warm leads can’t be saved without key details; lead assignment rules; and reports that tie lead source to closed deals.
Can Salesforce calculate MAO?
Yes. A formula field can calculate MAO from ARV, your percentage and repair costs on every deal, so every rep uses the same math.
Is Salesforce Starter enough for a wholesaler?
Usually not. Starter allows 0 custom objects, so you can’t add Property, Offer or Buyer objects, and Salesforce doesn’t state API access for it on its pages.
How many flows does Salesforce Professional allow?
Salesforce’s Professional Edition allocation page lists 5 flows. Enterprise and Unlimited allow 4,000 total and 2,000 active.
Can I track who changed a lead’s stage in Salesforce?
Yes. Field history tracking records the old value, new value, user and time for up to 20 fields per object, kept 18 months in the interface without Field Audit Trail.
Does Salesforce work offline for driving for dollars?
The mobile app caches recent records and Offline Edit lets users create and edit records offline, syncing when the device reconnects.

## Free Real Estate Salesforce Health Check (10 Points)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-health-check.html

Is your Salesforce a weapon — or just a bill?
The Real Estate Salesforce Health Check is a 10-point scorecard I use at the start of every engagement. Answer the ten yes/no questions below and you'll know exactly where your CRM is leaking deals, hours, and money.
Speed to lead: Does every new lead reach a rep within 5 minutes, automatically, at any hour? Fix: speed to lead guide →
Lead routing: Are leads assigned by rules (round robin, market, source) instead of someone forwarding emails? Fix: lead routing →
Pipeline truth: Can leadership see an accurate pipeline without asking anyone to update a spreadsheet? Fix: pipeline dashboard →
Adoption: Does almost everyone log calls, notes and stage changes in Salesforce, not in their phones? Fix: adoption fixes →
Automation health: Do your automations run on native Salesforce Flow rather than a tangle of third-party zaps? Fix: 15 automation recipes →
Call logging: Are calls logged automatically from your phone system, with no manual entry? Fix: dialers in Salesforce →
Campaign ROI: Do you know cost per lead and cost per closed deal for every channel? Fix: cost per deal calculator →
Deal profitability: Can you see net profit per deal, including all costs, inside the CRM? Fix: deal profit in Salesforce →
Duplicates and data: Is duplicate detection automated, and do you trust the data enough to decide from it? Fix: data quality features →
Stale leads: Does the system escalate leads nobody has touched in 48 hours? Fix: report recipes →
Score: 9–10, your CRM is working for you. 6–8, solid but hours and deals are slipping. 0–5, it costs more than it returns, and every point is fixable. The PDF version is below for printing or sharing with your team.
