## Salesforce Integrations for Real Estate Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-integrations-real-estate.html

Salesforce integrations for real estate investors.
Salesforce connects to almost every tool investors use , including DocuSign, QuickBooks, RingCentral, Gmail, Facebook lead ads, Google Ads and Slack, through AppExchange packages, the API or tools like Zapier. Below: what each connection syncs, which edition it needs, and what it changes for a wholesaling team.
Most investor tools connect to Salesforce through an AppExchange package or the API. The API is on by default only in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer ; Professional needs an add-on. Check this first. source
The connections that change results most for wholesalers: phone and text logging , lead source capture , e-signature on the deal and accounting for assignment fees .
Open CTI, which many dialers use inside Salesforce, reaches end of life on February 28, 2028. Ask any dialer vendor what their plan is. source
Zapier and Make are fine for one-way hops. For two-way sync (accounting) or in-app features (click to dial, signing), use a native package.
Jump to: The matrix Before you connect Tool by tool Native or Zapier What to connect first Questions
Which tools connect to Salesforce, and what changes when they do?
One row per tool category an investor or wholesaling team typically runs. The “what changes” column is what I set up for real estate teams; the rest is from each vendor’s own documentation, linked under Sources.
Category | Connector (who builds it) | What syncs | Edition or requirement | What changes for a wholesaler | Deep dive
E-signature | Docusign eSignature for Salesforce (by Docusign) | Send from the record with fields merged into a template; signed PDF and signer data written back | Works on Professional and up, per Salesforce | Purchase and assignment contracts live on the deal; a signed contract can move the stage | DocuSign guide
Accounting | Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato (third party) | Invoices, payments and customers; direction depends on the connector | Ask the vendor; API access is likely to matter | Assignment fees invoiced from the deal; paid status visible in Salesforce | QuickBooks guide
Email and calendar | Gmail and Outlook integration, Einstein Activity Capture (by Salesforce) | Side panel logging; automatic contact and event sync | EAC Standard in Starter through Enterprise | Buyer and title emails land on the right record without copy-paste | —
Phone / dialer | RingCentral, Aircall, Dialpad, Twilio Flex, Salesforce Voice | Click to dial, screen pop, call logging, recordings | RingCentral: Professional+. Aircall and Dialpad: Enterprise or Unlimited | Calls per rep and contact rate per list without manual notes | Dialer guide
Texting | Dialpad or RingCentral SMS, SMS-Magic, Twilio for Salesforce (beta), Salesforce Messaging | Texts logged to the lead; opt-outs tracked | 10DLC registration required for app-to-person texting in the US | Seller texts in the same timeline as calls; STOP respected | Texting guide
Lead sources | Web-to-Lead, Lead Capture for Facebook, Google Ads Conversion Import, CallRail | New leads in; for Google Ads, contract stages back out as conversions | Web-to-Lead: 500 leads/day. Google Ads and CallRail need API access | Every lead has a source; ads optimize for contracts, not form fills | Lead sources guide
List data / skip tracing | PropStream export, BatchData API, BatchLeads via Zapier | Spreadsheet import, or custom API calls | No native Salesforce connector found for PropStream or BatchData | Skip-trace results and DNC flags written to the lead | —
Files | Files Connect (Google Drive, OneDrive, Box), Box for Salesforce | External files browsed and shared from Salesforce | Google Drive source: Professional and up | One folder per deal: photos, repair estimate, title, contracts | —
Team chat | Salesforce for Slack apps, Slack actions in Flow | Record alerts in channels; approvals in Slack | Salesforce Channels: Starter and up | #dispo gets the deal the minute it goes under contract | —
Scheduling | Calendly package (by Calendly) | Bookings create or update leads and events | Enterprise or higher, per Calendly | Walkthrough bookings land on the seller lead | —
Maps | Salesforce Maps (add-on), Geopointe (Ascent Cloud) | Leads and deals on a map; routes; radius search | Add-on; bundled in Agentforce 1 Sales | Driving-for-dollars routes from your own lead data | —
Email marketing | Account Engagement (Pardot); Mailchimp via Beaufort 12 | Two-way sync of prospects and email activity | Account Engagement: Professional and up | New-deal emails to buyers segmented by buy box; engagement on the contact | —
Glue | Zapier, Make, Workato | Trigger in one app, action in another | Zapier Salesforce is a premium app; API limits apply | Connects tools that have no native connector | Zapier guide
What do you need before connecting anything?
1. API access
Salesforce says API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer, and that Professional can add it as an add-on. CallRail, Calendly, Dialpad, Aircall and Google Ads all depend on it, and Calendly says Group and Professional editions “cause errors.” source · Calendly
2. A dedicated integration user
Each connection should log in as its own user with only the permissions it needs, so you can see what it changed and switch it off without breaking anything else. Salesforce offers an API-only Integration user license for system-to-system connections. source
3. Fields that the integration writes to
Decide where each value lands before you install: call outcome, lead source, GCLID, contract status, invoice status. If the field doesn’t exist, the data ends up in a note nobody reports on. The CRM field kit has the core list.
4. A test in a sandbox (when the connector supports it)
Google’s Salesforce conversion import does not support sandboxes, so test that one with a single campaign in production. source
5. Token limits
Zapier notes that Salesforce allows 5 access tokens per account across third-party apps, and a sixth silently revokes the oldest. Another reason to give each integration its own user. source
Tool by tool: what each integration does for an investor
DocuSign: contracts signed from the deal
Docusign’s own package sends agreements from Salesforce using templates that pull record fields through merge fields, and writes signed documents and signer data back to Salesforce. Salesforce lists it as working with Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Starter and Performance. For a wholesaler that means the purchase agreement and the assignment contract go out from the same deal record, and the signed copies stay there. source · Full DocuSign guide
QuickBooks: assignment fees you can report on
The common QuickBooks connectors are third party: Breadwinner and DBSync (packages) or Workato (integration platform). Breadwinner creates invoices from Opportunities, Accounts or custom objects and tracks paid, overdue and due status. DBSync maps Opportunity to Invoice, Sales Receipt or Credit Memo. Breadwinner · DBSync · Full QuickBooks guide
Gmail and Outlook: no more copy-pasting emails
Salesforce’s Gmail and Outlook integrations add a side panel to log emails and create records. Einstein Activity Capture syncs contacts and events automatically. Salesforce for Outlook, the old desktop plug-in, retires in December 2027. source
Dialers: every call on the lead
RingCentral supports Professional and above; Aircall and Dialpad require Enterprise or Unlimited. All log calls to Salesforce records. Several, including RingCentral and Twilio Flex, use Open CTI, which ends February 28, 2028, with Salesforce Voice as the recommended replacement. RingCentral · Aircall · Dialpad · Full dialer guide
Texting: compliant before it’s fast
Twilio states that anyone sending app-to-person texts over a 10DLC number to the US must register for A2P 10DLC. Salesforce’s own messaging retired its standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026, and US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks. Twilio · Salesforce · Full texting guide
Lead sources: every lead tagged where it came from
Web-to-Lead takes up to 500 leads a day from your website. Lead Capture imports Facebook lead forms (Professional and up). Google’s Conversion Import for Salesforce sends stage changes back to Google Ads, so ads optimize toward contracts. CallRail sends call data only; texts and form fills don’t reach Salesforce. Web-to-Lead · Facebook · Google Ads · CallRail · Full lead sources guide
PropStream and BatchData: lists and skip tracing
PropStream exports lead lists as a spreadsheet; I found no Salesforce integration on its pages. BatchData offers a skip tracing API that returns phones flagged mobile or landline, plus DNC and TCPA litigator checks, but no Salesforce connector, so connecting it is a custom callout or middleware job. PropStream · BatchData
Google Drive, OneDrive and Box: one folder per deal
Salesforce Files Connect lets users browse and share files from Google Drive, SharePoint/OneDrive and Box inside Salesforce. Box for Salesforce adds a Box folder on each record. Files Connect · Box
Slack: the team hears about contracts instantly
Salesforce builds the current Slack apps, including Sales Cloud for Slack, Approvals in Slack and Flow actions that post to channels. source
Calendly: walkthroughs booked onto the lead
The Calendly package creates or updates Salesforce records when someone books; if it can’t match an email it creates a new lead. It requires Enterprise or higher and a Calendly Teams plan or above. source
Salesforce Maps: driving for dollars from your own data
Plots records on a map with routes, territories and nearby search. It’s an add-on, bundled in Agentforce 1 Sales. source
Email marketing: buyer blasts that report back
Account Engagement syncs with Professional and higher every 2–4 minutes. Mailchimp’s current Salesforce integration is built by Beaufort 12. Account Engagement · Mailchimp
Native package or Zapier?
Need | Use | Why
Click to dial, embedded signing, a panel on the record | Native package | Zapier and Make don’t add anything inside the Salesforce screen
Two-way sync (invoices and payments) | Native package or Workato | Conflict handling and status updates both ways
“When a lead is tagged in tool X, create it in Salesforce” | Zapier or Make | Fast to set up for one-way hops
Near-instant reaction | Native package, or a Salesforce outbound message | Most Zapier Salesforce triggers are polling; the instant one is New Outbound Message
Zapier lists Salesforce as a premium app and says Salesforce API limits apply. source · common problems
What should a wholesaling team connect first?
1. Phone and text
Most seller conversations happen here. If calls and texts aren’t on the lead, nothing downstream (follow-up, reporting, coaching) works.
2. Lead sources
Web forms, Facebook, PPC and call tracking, each tagged with a source. Without this you can’t compute cost per deal .
3. E-signature
Contracts on the deal, and a signed contract moving the stage.
4. Accounting
Once deals close regularly: assignment fees invoiced from the deal, so reports show realized revenue.
5. Everything else
Slack alerts, maps, buyer email, scheduling. Useful, but they don’t fix a leak by themselves.
Questions
Does Salesforce integrate with DocuSign?
Yes. Docusign publishes Docusign eSignature for Salesforce on AppExchange. It sends agreements from Salesforce records using templates with merge fields and writes signed documents back. It needs a separate Docusign subscription.
Does Salesforce integrate with QuickBooks?
Yes, commonly through third-party connectors such as Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato, or through Zapier. They sync invoices, payments and customers between QuickBooks Online and Salesforce.
Which Salesforce edition do I need for integrations?
Many connectors need API access, which is included in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer, and is an add-on for Professional. Some, such as DocuSign and RingCentral, also work on Professional. Check each vendor’s requirements.
Can I connect PropStream to Salesforce?
I found no native PropStream integration with Salesforce. PropStream exports lists as spreadsheets, which you can import with the Data Import Wizard (up to 50,000 records at a time) or Data Loader.
What is happening to Open CTI?
Salesforce says Open CTI reaches end of life on February 28, 2028, and existing implementations stop working after that. Salesforce Voice is the recommended replacement. Dialer vendors that use Open CTI need a new path.
Is Zapier enough to connect my real estate tools to Salesforce?
For simple one-way steps, often yes. For two-way sync, in-app features like click to dial, or near-instant updates, a native package is usually the better fit.

## Get Every Real Estate Lead Source into Salesforce
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-lead-sources-real-estate.html

Every lead source into Salesforce, tagged.
Real estate investors get leads into Salesforce through Web-to-Lead for website forms, Lead Capture for Facebook lead ads, CallRail for calls, and imports for lists . Google Ads can then learn from which leads became contracts. Here’s each route, what it needs, and the rules that keep the source on the record to the closed deal.
Web-to-Lead turns your website form into Salesforce leads, up to 500 a day. source
Lead Capture imports Facebook lead forms into Sales Cloud (Professional and up). source
Google Ads Conversion Import for Salesforce sends contract stages back to Google Ads, so ads learn which clicks became contracts. source
CallRail sends call data only; texts and form submissions don’t report to Salesforce. source
How does each lead source get into Salesforce?
Source | Route | What lands in Salesforce | Requirement
Website form | Web-to-Lead | A lead, optionally tied to a campaign; auto-response email | 500 leads per day; reCAPTCHA on by default
Facebook lead ads | Salesforce Lead Capture; or Meta’s partner integrations, webhooks or Zapier | A lead mapped from the lead form fields | Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited or Developer; admin on the Facebook Page
Google Ads | Web-to-Lead with a hidden GCLID field, then Conversion Import for Salesforce | The lead with its GCLID; later, stage changes go back to Google Ads | API enabled; GCLID field on Lead and Opportunity; field history on status/stage
Call tracking | CallRail integration | Calls with source, campaign, keywords, UTM, GCLID, recording, transcript; new leads when no match | REST API access
Lists (PropStream, county) | Spreadsheet → Data Import Wizard or Data Loader | Leads with list name as source | Wizard: 50,000 rows at a time
Sources: Web-to-Lead · Facebook import · Lead Capture requirements · Meta · Google Ads · setup · CallRail · CallRail fields · PropStream
Why connect Google Ads to Salesforce?
Without it, Google Ads optimizes toward form fills, and a tire-kicker counts the same as a motivated seller. With Conversion Import, you send “Under Contract” or “Closed” stage changes back as conversions, so bidding favors the keywords that produce contracts. Google’s requirements: the API enabled, a 255-character GCLID field on Lead and Opportunity mapped on conversion, field history tracking on lead status or opportunity stage, auto-tagging, and a hidden GCLID field on your form. Clicks older than 90 days aren’t imported, and the legacy integration lost support on May 31, 2025. source · legacy
What rules keep lead sources clean?
One picklist, set automatically
Lead source is a picklist, set by the form, the integration or the import, never typed. Free text breaks every report.
Source survives conversion
Map lead source and GCLID from Lead to the deal. If the source is lost at contract, cost per deal becomes a guess.
Duplicates merge, sources don’t vanish
The same seller from a mailer and a web form: keep the first source, record the second touch. Duplicate rules can alert or block.
Every new lead gets a task
A Flow assigns and creates a call task within minutes; see the speed to lead guide .
Questions
How do I get Facebook leads into Salesforce?
Salesforce Lead Capture can import Facebook lead forms into Sales Cloud on Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited and Developer editions. Meta also documents partner CRM integrations, webhooks and its Graph API.
Can Google Ads optimize for signed contracts from Salesforce?
Yes. Google Ads Conversion Import for Salesforce imports lead status or opportunity stage changes as conversions. It needs a GCLID field, field history tracking and API access.
Does CallRail send texts to Salesforce?
No. CallRail says text messages and form submissions don’t report to Salesforce; only call data does.
How many leads can Web-to-Lead capture?
Salesforce Help says up to 500 leads per 24 hours. Extra requests wait in a pending queue and you can ask Support for an increase.

## QuickBooks + Salesforce for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-quickbooks-real-estate.html

QuickBooks + Salesforce for real estate investors.
QuickBooks Online connects to Salesforce through third-party connectors like Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato , which sync invoices, payments and customers. For investors, the payoff is assignment fees invoiced from the deal and paid status in Salesforce reports, so you see realized revenue and cost per deal by lead source.
The common QuickBooks connectors are third party: Breadwinner and DBSync (packages) or Workato and Zapier (integration platforms). Breadwinner · DBSync · Workato
For investors the point is realized revenue on the deal : the assignment fee invoiced from Salesforce, and paid status visible in Salesforce reports.
Mapping fees and marketing costs is a design decision. No connector does it out of the box.
Which QuickBooks connectors work with Salesforce?
Connector | Type | What syncs (per the vendor) | Notes
Breadwinner for QuickBooks | AppExchange package (third party) | Two-way sync of invoices and customers; invoice status (paid, overdue, due); payments; bills and purchase orders. Invoices can be created from Opportunities, Accounts, Orders or custom objects. | QuickBooks Online. One vendor screen calls QuickBooks data “read-only inside Salesforce”, so confirm direction per object.
DBSync | Package plus scheduler (third party) | Accounts/Contacts ↔ Customers, Products ↔ Items, Opportunity ↔ Invoice, Sales Receipt or Credit Memo; history migration | Sync by buttons or schedule. Opportunities need an Account and Standard Price Book products.
Workato | Integration platform | QuickBooks Online: 27 triggers, 87 actions. Salesforce: 16 triggers, 36 actions. | Most flexible; you design each recipe.
Zapier / Make | Integration platform | One-way “when X, do Y” steps | Good for simple hops; weaker for two-way accounting sync.
Sources: Breadwinner · DBSync · Workato . None of these pages states a minimum Salesforce edition; ask the vendor, and expect API access to matter. API editions
What should an investor track across Salesforce and QuickBooks?
Number | Lives in | Why it matters
Contract price, assignment price, assignment fee | Salesforce (deal) | The fee is a formula on the deal, so every report uses the same math
Invoice for the fee, paid date | QuickBooks, status synced to Salesforce | Separates fees you expect from fees you collected
Marketing spend by campaign | QuickBooks bills, totals pushed to Salesforce campaigns | Lets Salesforce compute cost per deal by source
Closing costs on double closes | Salesforce (deal) | What you actually kept; see double closing costs
Cancelled or renegotiated contracts | Salesforce (deal) | Fall-outs come out of campaign ROI
What does the flow look like for a wholesaler?
1. Deal closes in Salesforce
Stage moves to Closed. The assignment fee is already on the deal as a formula.
2. Invoice created
The connector creates a QuickBooks invoice to the end buyer or title company for the fee, from the deal.
3. Payment comes back
When QuickBooks shows it paid, the status updates on the deal. A “Closed – Paid” report shows realized fees by month and by lead source.
4. Spend meets revenue
Monthly marketing totals by campaign (mailers, PPC, skip tracing) land on Salesforce campaigns, and cost per deal becomes a report instead of a spreadsheet.
Questions
Does Salesforce integrate with QuickBooks Online?
Yes. The common routes are third-party connectors such as Breadwinner and DBSync, integration platforms such as Workato, or Zapier.
Can Salesforce create QuickBooks invoices from a deal?
Breadwinner says invoices can be created from Opportunities, Accounts, Orders or custom objects, and DBSync maps Opportunities to invoices, sales receipts or credit memos.
Should my accountant work in Salesforce?
No. Keep the books in QuickBooks. Sync only what Salesforce needs for reporting: invoice status, paid date and campaign spend totals.
Can I see profit per lead source in Salesforce?
Yes, if assignment fees live on the deal, the deal keeps its lead source, and marketing spend is recorded on campaigns. Then a report can show fees and cost per deal by source.

## 20 Salesforce Reports for Wholesalers (Recipes)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-reports-wholesalers.html

20 Salesforce reports for a wholesaling team.
The Salesforce reports that matter most to wholesalers show where leads come from, how fast they’re called, which offers become contracts, and what each source costs per closed deal. Here are 20 report recipes written as report type, filter, grouping and measure, the limits to know, and which five belong on the Monday dashboard.
These are 20 reports a wholesaling team can build in Salesforce, written as report type → filter → group by → measure , so you or your admin can build them in an afternoon.
Three features make them possible: custom report types (Property, Offer, Buyer), cross filters (“leads without activities”) and reporting snapshots (trends over time). source · snapshots
Most need fields that exist and are filled in: lead source as a picklist, call outcome, MAO, contract and assignment price, dead reason. Start with the CRM field kit .
20 reports for a wholesaling team
Report | Report type | Filter | Group by | Measure | Answers
Leads by source this month | Leads | Created date = this month | Lead source | Count | Monday 5
Speed to first contact | Leads with activities | Created last 30 days | Owner | Average minutes from created to first call (formula field) | Speed to lead
Leads with no activity in 7 days | Leads with or without activities (cross filter: without activities in 7 days) | Status not dead | Owner | Count | Follow-up
Missed inbound calls and callback time | Tasks / call logs | Direction inbound, outcome missed, last 7 days | Day, campaign | Count; avg callback minutes | Missed calls
Call outcomes by caller | Tasks | Type = call, last 7 days | Caller, outcome | Count | Coaching
Contact rate by list | Leads with activities | Source = list | List name | Contacted ÷ dialed (summary formula) | Lists
Appointments by campaign | Opportunities or events | Created this month | Campaign | Count; cost per appointment | Monday 5
Offers made vs contracts signed | Offers with deals (custom report type) | Offer date this month | Rep | Offers; contracts; ratio | Offer discipline
Offers above MAO | Offers | Offer amount > MAO (formula flag) | Rep | Count | Offer discipline
Pipeline by stage | Opportunities | Open | Stage | Count; expected fee | Pipeline
Days in stage | Opportunities with field history | Open | Stage | Average days (from stage history) | Bottlenecks
Contract to first TC call | Opportunities with activities | Under contract this month | TC | Average hours | Closing
Cost per closed deal by source | Campaigns with opportunities | Closed this quarter, fall-outs excluded | Lead source | Spend ÷ closed deals | Cost per deal
Booked vs realized fees | Opportunities | Closed this quarter | Month | Expected fee; actual fee; difference | Revenue
Fall-outs by reason | Opportunities | Stage = cancelled | Dead reason, source | Count | Honest ROI
Dead leads with re-contact date this week | Leads | Status = not now, re-contact date = this week | Owner | Count | Long follow-up
Days from contract to assignment | Opportunities | Assigned this quarter | Dispo rep | Average days | Dispo
Buyers who closed in 12 months | Buyers with deals (custom report type) | Closed in last 12 months | Buyer | Deals; total paid | Buyer list
Who changed lead source | Lead history | Field = lead source | User | Count | Data trust
Weekly pipeline trend | Reporting snapshot object | Last 12 weeks | Week | Pipeline value | Trend
What Salesforce report limits should you know?
Item | Limit
Rows shown in a report | 2,000 in the interface; export for more
Custom report types | Professional 50, Enterprise 300, Unlimited 2,000
Objects in one custom report type | Up to 60 object references, 1,000 fields
Joined reports | Enterprise and up, up to 5 blocks
Cross filters | Up to 3 per report
Dashboard components | Up to 25 per dashboard
Reporting snapshots | Professional and up; 200 in Professional
Field history | 20 fields per object, 18 months in the interface
Sources: limits · report types · joined reports · snapshots · field history
Which reports belong on the Monday dashboard?
Five, not twenty: leads by source, speed to first contact, offers vs contracts, cost per closed deal by source, and pipeline by stage. Everything else is for drilling in when a number moves. The reasoning and formulas are in the Monday 5 ; layout ideas in the pipeline dashboard guide .
Why do CRM reports get ignored?
Usually because nobody trusts the data. In Validity’s 2025 survey of 602 CRM users, 76% said less than half of their CRM data is accurate and complete. source The fix is upstream: picklists instead of free text, validation rules at each stage, lead source locked after creation, and a “who changed it” report so problems are visible.
Questions
What reports should a wholesaler run in Salesforce?
Start with leads by source, speed to first contact, leads with no activity in 7 days, offers vs contracts by rep, cost per closed deal by source and pipeline by stage.
How do I report on leads with no activity in Salesforce?
Use a cross filter: leads without activities, with a date condition such as the last 7 days. Salesforce allows up to 3 cross filters per report.
Can Salesforce show trends over time?
Yes. Reporting snapshots save a report’s results to a custom object on a schedule, so you can chart weekly pipeline or lead counts.
Why can I only see 2,000 rows in a Salesforce report?
The report interface shows up to 2,000 rows. Export the report to see all rows, or summarize with groupings.

## Texting Sellers from Salesforce: 10DLC and Consent
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-texting-real-estate.html

Texting sellers from Salesforce: 10DLC, consent and tools.
To text sellers from Salesforce in the US, you need a texting tool that logs to Salesforce, a registered 10DLC brand and campaign, and consent and opt-out fields every tool respects. Here are the tools, the registration steps, what CTIA’s guidelines say about lists, and how I set up the fields. This is not legal advice.
Twilio: “Anyone sending SMS/MMS messages over a 10DLC number from an application to the US must register for A2P 10DLC.” Registration has a brand and a campaign. source
CTIA’s guidelines say marketing texts need express written consent and senders “should not use rented, sold, or shared lists.” That matters for skip-traced lists. source
Salesforce retired its standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026; US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks. source
How can you text sellers from Salesforce?
Option | Built by | What it does | Watch out for
Dialpad or RingCentral | Dialer vendor | Texts from the dialer, logged to Salesforce | Dialpad logs SMS to the contact, not opportunities or shared lines
SMS-Magic Converse | SMS-Magic | Salesforce-native SMS, MMS, WhatsApp; templates, keyword auto-replies, campaigns, opt-in/opt-out tracking | Confirm current product naming with the vendor
Twilio for Salesforce | Twilio | 1:1 and bulk SMS from records; inbox component | Public beta, not covered by a Twilio SLA
Salesforce Messaging (enhanced SMS) | Salesforce | Native SMS channel in Service Cloud messaging | Standard channels retired Feb 14, 2026; registration takes 1–4 weeks
Sources: Dialpad · RingCentral · SMS-Magic · Twilio for Salesforce · Salesforce
What is 10DLC and do investors need it?
10DLC is the US system for business texting from regular 10-digit numbers. Twilio says anyone sending app-to-person texts over a 10DLC number to the US must register, including individuals. You register a brand (who is sending; standard brands need a business tax ID) and a campaign (the use case and your opt-in, opt-out and help messages). Registered traffic gets less filtering and more throughput. source
The Campaign Registry runs the registry behind it; brands register through a provider such as Twilio, not directly. source
What do the industry rules say about texting lists?
CTIA guidance (May 2023) | What it means for a wholesaler
Marketing messages need express written consent | A seller who filled out your form and agreed to texts is different from a number on a list
Honor STOP and plain-language opt-outs, one confirmation, then nothing | Opt-out must be a field in Salesforce that every texting tool respects
Don’t use rented, sold or shared lists | Bulk-texting a purchased or skip-traced list conflicts with this guidance
CTIA’s document is voluntary industry guidance, not a substitute for TCPA advice. Talk to a lawyer before you text lists. source
How should Salesforce store texting data?
Consent: a checkbox plus date and source (“web form, October 2026”). No consent, no marketing texts.
Opt-out: one field every tool checks before sending, set automatically when someone replies STOP.
Every text on the timeline: calls and texts in one history, so the next rep sees the whole conversation.
DNC and litigator flags from your skip-tracing provider, if it returns them. BatchData’s API returns DNC and TCPA litigator checks. source
Questions
Do I need 10DLC registration to text sellers?
Twilio says anyone sending app-to-person SMS over a 10DLC number to the US must register for A2P 10DLC. Toll-free numbers and short codes are separate systems.
Can I text a skip-traced list from Salesforce?
CTIA’s guidelines call for express written consent for marketing texts and say senders should not use rented, sold or shared lists. Get legal advice on the TCPA before texting lists.
What happened to Salesforce’s standard SMS channels?
Salesforce retired standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026. New channels are enhanced, and US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks.
Can texts and calls show in one Salesforce timeline?
Yes, if your dialer or texting tool logs both to the same record. Dialpad logs SMS as completed tasks on the contact; RingCentral logs calls and messages.

## Salesforce Access for VAs and Cold Callers
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-va-access-real-estate.html

Salesforce access for VAs and cold callers.
Real estate teams can give VAs and cold callers exactly the Salesforce access they need with profiles, permission sets, sharing rules and field-level security, and protect the lead list by removing export rights. Here’s what each role should see, which features do it, and a VA onboarding and offboarding checklist.
Most investor teams have VAs and cold callers, often in other countries. Salesforce lets you give them exactly the access they need: permission sets , sharing rules and field-level security . permission sets
Salesforce enforces multi-factor authentication for all employee logins; production enforcement rolled out July 20 to September 3, 2026. Plan it into VA onboarding. source
Field history tracking shows who changed what, for up to 20 fields per object. source
What should each role see?
Role | Can | Can’t
Cold caller / VA | Create and edit leads in their queue; log calls; set outcome and next date | See deal financials, buyer list, exports, other markets
Acquisitions rep | Own leads and deals; make offers; send contracts | Change lead source after creation; delete records
Dispo rep | See under-contract deals and buyers; send deals; log buyer offers | See seller notes beyond what’s needed
Transaction coordinator | Closing tasks, documents, dates | Edit offer or assignment amounts
Owner / manager | Everything, including reports and fees | —
Which Salesforce security features do this?
Feature | What it does | Edition / limit
Profiles | Default settings for each user; one profile per user | Custom profiles in Professional and up
Permission sets and groups | Add permissions on top of a profile; Salesforce’s recommended approach | All main editions
Sharing rules | Open record access beyond org-wide defaults, by owner or criteria | Professional and up; up to 300 per object
Field-level security | Hide or make read-only specific fields, across UI, reports and API | Professional and up
Login IP ranges | Deny logins from outside set ranges | Per profile in Enterprise and up; Professional needs an add-on for per-profile ranges
MFA | Second factor for every employee login; phishing-resistant for admins | Enforced in 2026
Field history tracking | Who changed a field, from what, to what, when | 20 fields per object; 18 months in the UI
Sources: profiles · permission sets · sharing rules · field-level security · login IP ranges · MFA · field history
A VA onboarding and offboarding checklist
Before day one
Create the user with the caller profile and permission set; add to the right queue; confirm MFA method; share the call script and the handoff rules .
First week
Review their call outcomes daily; check the fields they skip; fix the layout before blaming the person.
Ongoing
Weekly calibration: compare their warm and hot leads with what acquisitions found.
Offboarding (same day)
Freeze then deactivate the user; reassign open leads and tasks to the queue; revoke integrations or dialer seats tied to them.
How do you protect your lead list?
Remove the export permission from caller and VA profiles; only owners export.
Give VAs list views, not report builder access, if they don’t need it.
Track changes to lead source, phone and owner with field history.
Keep integration users separate from people, so a departing VA can’t take an API connection with them. API access itself is included in Enterprise and an add-on for Professional. source
Questions
How do I give a VA limited access in Salesforce?
Give them a restricted profile plus a permission set with only what they need, hide sensitive fields with field-level security, and use queues and sharing rules so they see only their leads.
Does Salesforce require MFA for VAs?
Salesforce enforces multi-factor authentication for all employee logins, with production enforcement rolled out from July 20 to September 3, 2026.
Can I stop VAs exporting my leads?
Yes. Export is a permission; leave it off caller and VA profiles and permission sets so only owners can export.

## Salesforce vs GoHighLevel for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-vs-gohighlevel.html

Salesforce vs GoHighLevel for investors.
GoHighLevel is a marketing platform with a CRM inside. Salesforce is a CRM platform you shape to your process. Neither has wholesaling data built in. Here’s how they compare, with every claim linked to the source.
GoHighLevel is a marketing platform: funnels, sites, texting, calling and workflows, billed by plan plus usage.
Salesforce is a CRM platform you configure: custom records, reporting, permissions and a large app marketplace.
Neither has wholesaling data (lists, skip tracing, cash buyers) built in. Both need a data tool next to them.
Disclosure: I build Salesforce CRMs for investors, so I have a bias. To keep it in check, every feature and price below comes from the vendor’s own site, linked in the row. I don’t list Salesforce prices: most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive based on the business and number of users.
Side by side
 | GoHighLevel | Salesforce
Built for | Agencies and small businesses; real estate page targets agents and brokerages source · real estate page | Businesses of any size source
Investor features | Property Investor bundle of templates, funnels and workflows source | None out of the box; you build Property, Offer and Buyer records
Calling and texting | Built in, usage-billed phone pricing | Add-on or AppExchange apps source
Funnels and sites | Built in | Not native; use your site and web-to-lead
Skip tracing and lists | Not built in | Not native; connect a data tool BatchLeads
Custom records | Custom objects source | Custom objects on Professional and up (Starter: custom fields only, 25 per object) source
Reports | Reporting; agent reporting on Agency Pro source | Custom reports and dashboards; field history tracking on chosen fields. Report recipes
API | Basic on Unlimited, Advanced on Agency Pro source | Enterprise and up; add-on for Professional source
Price | Starter $97, Unlimited $297, Agency Pro $497 a month plus usage. Published price, read from the vendor’s site in October 2026. Prices change; check the link. | Quoted. Most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive.
GoHighLevel’s usage fees
HighLevel bills phone and text by usage on top of the plan. Its help center lists US rates per minute and per text segment, plus A2P 10DLC registration and monthly campaign fees for texting. Budget for these at your volume, not just the plan price. HighLevel phone pricing
Where GoHighLevel wins
Marketing in one place. Funnels, sites, texting, email and calling in one tool.
Predictable plan price for the platform itself, with unlimited users on Starter.
Fast to launch if you use a template or snapshot.
Where Salesforce wins
Data model. A deal with several offers, a property with several sellers, a buyer with a buy box, each a related record with its own validation and automation.
Reporting and audit trail. Who changed the offer price, and when. 37 features investors use
Integrations. DocuSign, QuickBooks, dialers and data tools. Integrations guide
Governance. Sandboxes to test changes, permissions by team and market.
Running both
Some teams keep GoHighLevel for funnels and texting campaigns and send leads into Salesforce as the system of record. It works if you decide which system owns each field and sync only one way for most of them. Otherwise you get two versions of every seller.
Questions
Is GoHighLevel a good CRM for real estate investors?
It’s strong for funnels, texting and workflows. Skip tracing, list stacking and cash buyer search aren’t built in, and its real estate page targets agents and brokerages, so wholesalers usually add a data tool.
Is Salesforce better than GoHighLevel?
They solve different problems. GoHighLevel is a marketing platform; Salesforce is a CRM platform you configure. Salesforce is the better system of record when you need custom records, reports and permissions across a growing team.
How much does GoHighLevel cost?
HighLevel’s published plans in October 2026 are Starter $97, Unlimited $297 and Agency Pro $497 a month, with phone, text, email and AI billed by usage on top.
Can GoHighLevel and Salesforce work together?
Yes. One setup sends leads from GoHighLevel funnels into Salesforce. Decide which system owns each field before you connect them.

## Salesforce vs Investor CRMs (Podio, REsimpli and Others)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-vs-investor-crms.html

Salesforce vs investor CRMs: how far each one goes.
Investor CRMs like REsimpli come ready for wholesaling and are the faster start. Podio lets you build your own apps. Salesforce goes furthest on data model, automation, reporting and testing, but costs more and needs to be set up. The right pick depends on your team size, markets and the reports you need.
Side by side
What you need | Salesforce | Podio | Wholesaling CRMs

How far Salesforce goes
Your process, not a fixed pipeline
One object for each thing you track: lead, property, offer, contract, buyer and assignment, all linked. Enterprise allows 200 custom objects and 500 custom fields per object, far more than an investor team needs.
Automation without code
Flow runs when a record changes (contract signed, so title and dispo get tasks), on a schedule (every Monday, "not ready" leads come back) and for approvals (an offer over MAO needs a manager). See the automations I'd build first .
Any question as a report
Cost per closed deal by lead source, offers over MAO by rep, days from first call to contract. Joined reports put marketing spend and closed deals in one view; reporting snapshots save the pipeline weekly so you see the trend. See the pipeline dashboard .
Built to grow
Sandboxes to test changes before they go live, field history on up to 20 fields per object ( source ), access by team and market, a daily API allowance that starts at 100,000 requests on Enterprise ( source ), and AppExchange, which lists more than 7,000 apps and consulting partners ( source ).
When Salesforce is overkill
Stay with an investor CRM if
You're solo or a small team doing a few deals a month, and the built-in pipeline fits how you work.
Salesforce makes sense when
You run several teams or markets, you need reports your tool can't build, or your process doesn't fit their pipeline. It should pay for itself in deals you keep, so get a quote first: most businesses are offered a discount on list price.
Questions
Is Salesforce better than an investor CRM?
Not for everyone. An investor CRM is built for wholesaling out of the box and is quicker to start. Salesforce fits when you have several teams or markets, need reports your current tool cannot build, or your process does not fit a fixed pipeline. I build on Salesforce, so weigh my view with that in mind.
How much does Salesforce cost for a small investor team?
Salesforce lists per-user monthly prices on its pricing page, but most businesses don't pay list. Talk to a Salesforce account executive: many teams are offered a discount based on the business and the number of users. Setup is extra, whether you do it yourself or hire someone.
Can Salesforce do what Podio does?
Podio lets you build custom apps from its field types and link apps with relationship fields. Salesforce does the same with custom objects and lookup fields, and adds built-in Flow automation, joined reports, reporting snapshots and sandboxes for testing changes.
Do I need a developer to run Salesforce?
Not for most investor setups. Objects, fields, page layouts, Flow automations and reports are built with point-and-click tools. Code is only needed for unusual integrations or logic.
What is the first step if I want to compare?
Write your stages from new lead to closed on paper, list the five reports you want every Monday, and ask each vendor to show you that exact flow and those reports in a demo.

Salesforce vs REsimpli for wholesalers.
REsimpli is an investor CRM with the dialer, texting and data already inside. Salesforce is a CRM you build around your own process. Here’s where each one wins, with every claim linked to the vendor’s own page.
REsimpli gives a wholesaling team calling, texting, lists, skip tracing and buyer sites in one login, priced by team size.

Pick REsimpli if you want it working this week and your process fits its pipeline. Pick Salesforce if you have several reps, markets or entities, or need custom reports or permission rules beyond what REsimpli offers. Test it in the trial.

## Seller Lead Follow-Up Cadence Builder for Investors (Free)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/seller-follow-up-cadence.html

Seller follow-up cadence builder.
Silence is not a no. Pick how hot the lead is, the date you first spoke, and the channels you use. You get a dated touch plan you can follow by hand or import into your CRM as tasks. It is a starting template: adjust it to your market and your own results.
Your touch plan
# | Date | Day | Channel | Purpose
Rules that make any cadence work
Every open lead has a next touch date
A lead with no next task is a lead nobody will call. Make the next touch date required before a rep can save a call outcome.
Stop on a no, not on silence
Silence is not a no. Move a quiet lead to a slower cadence instead of closing it. Close it only when the seller says no, sells, or the property no longer fits, and record the reason.
Log channel and outcome on every touch
After a few hundred touches you can see which channel and which touch number actually gets replies, and replace guesses with your own numbers.
Re-rate the temperature after each conversation
A cold lead whose situation changes (a job move, a vacancy, a repair bill) becomes hot. Changing the temperature should restart the cadence from that date.
Questions
How many times should I follow up with a seller lead?
Until they say no or sell, not until you get tired. The cadence changes with the lead: a seller with a near deadline gets touches every few days, a seller who said "not now" gets a touch every month or quarter. What matters is that every open lead has a next touch date.
Should I call or text first?
Test it on your own list rather than guessing. Split a list in half, call first on one half and text first on the other, and compare reply rates after a few weeks. Log the channel on every touch so you can see the answer.
What is a hot, warm and cold seller lead?
In this builder, hot means a seller with a reason and a timeline under about a month, warm means interested but one to six months out, and cold means not now. Use your own definitions, but write them down so every rep labels leads the same way.
Is texting sellers legal?
Rules on texts and calls to consumers vary by country and US state, and several states are stricter than federal law. Check the rules that apply to you, and consent requirements, before you scale texting. This builder plans touches; it does not send anything.
How do I load the plan into my CRM?
Download the CSV and import it as tasks, or create the same steps as an automated cadence in your CRM. Most CRMs, including Salesforce, can create the next task automatically when the last one is completed.

## Speed to Lead for Real Estate Investors: The First-Hour Rule
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/speed-to-lead-real-estate-investors.html

Speed to lead for real estate investors: the first-hour rule.
Speed to lead is the time between a seller reaching out and a real person on your team talking to them. For investors and wholesalers it decides who gets the deal: motivated sellers usually contact several buyers, and they often go with the first one who answers and sounds able to help. Aim to reach every inbound lead within the hour, and measure it.
What the research says
The best-known study is The Short Life of Online Sales Leads (Harvard Business Review, March 2011) by James Oldroyd, Kristina McElheran and David Elkington. Looking at 1.25 million leads across 42 US companies, firms that contacted a lead within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify it as firms that waited longer, and more than 60 times as likely as firms that waited 24 hours or more. In a separate audit of 2,241 US companies, only 37% responded within an hour and 23% never responded.
That study covered web leads in general, not seller calls. A missed seller call is the same problem in a sharper form: the seller already reached out, and the clock is running against every other investor they called.
How to measure your speed to lead
Lead created time = when the call, form or text came in
First conversation time = when a person on your team actually spoke with the seller
Speed to lead (minutes) = first conversation time − lead created time
Report: median by lead source, by hour of day, and by rep, every Monday
Use the median, because one lead that waited three days will distort an average. Split by hour of day: most teams find their gap is evenings and weekends, which is when many sellers call.
Five rules that fix it in any CRM
1. Every missed call becomes a task
When a call to a marketing number is not answered, the CRM creates the lead if it does not exist and a callback task due in minutes. No missed call should exist only in the phone system.
2. Route to whoever is free
New leads and missed-call tasks go to the next available rep, not to the person who owns the number or the market. A lead waiting for one busy rep is a slow lead.
3. Escalate after 15 minutes
If nobody has touched a new lead or a callback task in 15 minutes, it moves to a second person or a manager. Pick the number that fits your team, then enforce it.
4. Acknowledge after hours, call first thing
Outside business hours, send the seller a short text that a person will call at a set time, then make that call the first task of the morning. Track the acknowledgment and the conversation as separate times.
5. Put the number on the Monday report
Median speed to lead and missed calls not returned, by source. What gets reviewed every week gets faster.
What it costs you
Put your own numbers into the free missed seller call cost calculator : inbound calls, the share you miss, the share you never reach, your conversion rates and average profit. It turns missed calls into lost deals and lost profit per month and per year.
Questions
What is speed to lead?
The time between a seller reaching out (a call, a web form, a text reply) and a real person on your team having a conversation with them. Measure it to the first conversation, not to the first automated text.
What is a good speed to lead for a wholesaler or home-buying company?
Under an hour is the bar the research supports, and in practice the goal is minutes for inbound calls and web forms during business hours. More important than a target is knowing your real number by lead source and by hour of day.
Does an automatic text count as a response?
It helps, because the seller knows they reached someone. But it is not a conversation. Track automated acknowledgment and first human conversation as two separate times.
How do I measure speed to lead if my CRM does not track it?
Add two date-time fields to the lead: when the lead came in and when the first real conversation happened. A formula field gives the minutes between them. Report the median, not the average, by source and by hour.
Why do missed calls matter so much?
A missed inbound call is a seller who already chose to call you. If nobody calls back fast, they talk to the next investor on their list, and the lead never shows up in your CRM at all, so your reports cannot see the loss.

## Wholesale Assignment Fee: Set It So the Deal Still Sells
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesale-assignment-fee.html

Wholesale assignment fee: set it from the buyer's margin.
An assignment fee is what a wholesaler is paid for assigning the purchase contract to a cash buyer. The fee that works is not a round number you pick in advance: it is whatever is left after the buyer's repairs, costs and required profit come out of the after-repair value, minus your contract price. Price it from the buyer's side and deals sell instead of sitting.
The max-fee formula
Buyer's costs = ARV × closing, holding and selling %
Buyer's profit = the profit active buyers in that market need on this kind of deal
Max fee = ARV − repairs − buyer's costs − buyer's profit − your contract price
If max fee is below the fee you need, renegotiate the contract price or pass
Worked example
Made-up numbers to show the math. A house has a $250,000 after-repair value and needs $40,000 of repairs. The buyer's closing, holding and selling costs run about 10% of ARV, so $25,000. Buyers in that area want around 15% of ARV in profit on a medium rehab, so $37,500. Your contract price is $130,000. Max fee = $250,000 − $40,000 − $25,000 − $37,500 − $130,000 = $17,500 . Ask $25,000 and the buyer's profit drops to $30,000; some will pass, and the ones who stay may try to renegotiate before closing.
Run your own numbers in the free wholesale deal analyzer : it shows your MAO, the room under it, the buyer's all-in cost and the buyer's profit and return after your fee.
Assign or double close?
An assignment is usually cheaper: one closing, and the fee is paid at that closing. A double close means you buy the property and resell it, often the same day, so you pay a second set of closing costs and may need transactional funding, but the buyer does not see your spread on the assignment paperwork. Compare the two with your numbers in the assignment vs double close calculator .
What to track in your CRM
Planned fee vs closed fee
Save the fee you expected when you went under contract and the fee that actually closed. The gap shows how often buyers push back and on which kinds of deals.
Fee by lead source and campaign
Average fee per closed deal by source tells you more than lead counts do. A source with fewer leads and bigger fees can beat a cheaper one.
Assignment or double close
A picklist on the deal, plus the extra closing costs on double closes, so the report shows what you actually kept.
Questions
What is an assignment fee?
The amount a wholesaler is paid for assigning their purchase contract with the seller to an end buyer. The buyer pays the seller the contract price and pays the wholesaler the fee, usually at closing.
How much is a typical assignment fee?
There is no standard amount. It depends on the spread between your contract price and what buyers in that market will pay. The useful question is not what is typical but how much fee this deal can carry while the buyer still makes the profit they need.
Does the buyer see my fee?
With an assignment, usually yes: the fee appears in the assignment agreement and on the settlement statement. If a large fee would put the buyer or seller off, a double close is the common alternative, at the cost of a second set of closing costs.
Is assigning a contract legal everywhere?
Rules on wholesaling, assignment and disclosure vary by state and change over time, and some purchase contracts forbid assignment. For example, Oklahoma's SB 1075, in effect since November 1, 2025, requires written disclosures to the seller and a two-business-day right to cancel. This page is not legal advice; check the contract and ask a local real estate attorney before you assign.
What should my CRM track about fees?
The fee on every closed deal, the fee you planned when you went under contract, the lead source and the campaign. That shows which sources produce the deals with the biggest fees and how often fees get cut before closing.

## Wholesale Deal Analyzer: MAO, Your Fee & the Buyer's Profit
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesale-deal-analyzer.html

Wholesale deal analyzer.
One sheet for one deal: your maximum allowable offer, how much room your contract price leaves, what your cash buyer pays, and whether there is still enough profit in it for them to close. A deal that only works for you does not close. Built for real estate investors in the United States, Canada, the UK and Europe. Pick your currency; the math is the same everywhere.
The formula
MAO = ARV × rule % − repairs − your fee
Room under MAO = MAO − your contract price
Price to buyer = contract price + your fee
Buyer all-in = price to buyer + repairs + (ARV × buyer costs %)
Buyer profit = ARV − buyer all-in
Buyer return on cost = buyer profit ÷ buyer all-in
Worked example
A house with a $250,000 ARV needs $40,000 of repairs. At a 70% rule and a $12,000 fee, MAO is $123,000. You contract at $115,000, which leaves $8,000 of room. Your buyer pays $127,000, spends $40,000 on repairs and $25,000 on closing, holding and selling, for an all-in of $192,000. Sold at ARV, the buyer keeps $58,000, a 30.2% return on cost.
Questions
What is a good assignment fee?
There is no fixed number. The fee works when the buyer still has enough profit to take the deal. A useful check is the buyer's return on cost after your fee: if it drops below what active buyers in your market accept, the fee is too big for that deal.
What is the 70% rule?
A rule of thumb that a buyer should pay no more than 70% of the after-repair value minus repairs. It leaves room for closing, holding and selling costs and the buyer's profit. It is a starting point, not a law: adjust the percentage to what buyers in your market actually pay.
Why check the buyer's profit, not just my MAO?
Your MAO tells you what to offer the seller. The buyer's profit tells you whether the deal will sell. Deals that clear your MAO but leave the buyer a thin margin are the ones that sit, get renegotiated or fall out.
Where should the ARV come from?
Recent sold comparables near the property with similar size, age and condition after repairs. Active listings and automated estimates are a cross-check, not the number.
Can my CRM run this on every deal?
Yes. Put ARV, repairs, rule %, fee and contract price on the deal record as fields and the results as formula fields, so every rep makes offers from the same math and every lost deal shows why.

## Wholesaling Cost Per Deal Calculator by Lead Source
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesaling-cost-per-deal-calculator.html

Wholesaling cost per deal, by lead source.
Put in last month's (or last quarter's) numbers for each marketing channel. The calculator shows cost per lead, cost per contract, cost per closed deal and ROI side by side, so you can see which channel is actually paying for itself. Nothing you type leaves your browser.
Channel | Spend ($) | Leads | Contracts | Closed deals | Gross profit ($)
Results
Channel | Cost / lead | Lead → contract | Cost / contract | Cost / deal | ROI
Enter spend and closed deals for at least one channel.
Gross profit = assignment fees or net profit from the closed deals that came from that channel. Example numbers are made up for illustration only.
How the numbers work
How do you calculate cost per deal in wholesaling?
Divide the total marketing spend for a channel by the number of deals that closed from that channel in the same period. Example: $6,000 on direct mail that produced 2 closed deals is a $3,000 cost per deal.
What is the difference between cost per contract and cost per deal?
Cost per contract divides spend by signed purchase contracts. Cost per deal divides spend by closed (funded) deals. The gap between them shows how many contracts fall out before closing.
How do you calculate marketing ROI per lead source?
ROI = (gross profit from closed deals − marketing spend) ÷ marketing spend. A channel with $20,000 of assignment fees on $5,000 of spend has a 300% ROI.
Where should these numbers come from?
From your CRM. Every lead needs a lead source, every contract and closed deal needs to be linked to the original lead, and spend needs to be logged per channel per month. If any link is missing, the numbers are guesses.
Why most wholesalers can't fill this in
The usual gap is attribution: leads come in from mail, PPC, cold calls and texts, but the closed deal is never tied back to the original lead source in the CRM. That's the first thing I check in a CRM Revenue Audit , and it's item four on the free Salesforce Health Check .

## Wholesaling CRM Glossary: ARV, MAO, Cost per Deal
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesaling-crm-glossary.html

Wholesaling & investor CRM glossary.
Plain-English definitions of the terms acquisitions and dispo teams use every day, and where it helps, what each one looks like inside a CRM.
Acquisitions (acq)
The part of an investor business that finds motivated sellers, qualifies them and gets properties under contract. In a CRM: Usually the lead and opportunity stages owned by acquisition reps.
After-repair value (ARV)
What a property should sell for once repairs are done, based on recent sold comps of similar renovated homes nearby. In a CRM: A currency field on the deal record that feeds the MAO formula.
Assignment contract
A contract that lets a wholesaler transfer their right to buy a property to an end buyer for a fee, instead of buying it themselves.
Assignment fee
The wholesaler's profit on an assigned deal: the difference between the end buyer's price and the wholesaler's contract price. In a CRM: Captured on the transaction so campaign ROI uses real profit.
Attribution (lead source attribution)
Tying every contract and closed deal back to the marketing channel and campaign that produced the original lead. In a CRM: Lead source carried from lead to opportunity to transaction and locked against accidental edits.
Booked revenue
Expected profit recorded when a deal goes under contract, before it closes. In a CRM: Compared weekly against what deals actually closed for (forecast vs. actual).
Comps (comparable sales)
Recently sold properties similar in size, age, condition and location, used to estimate ARV.
Contract-to-close rate
Closed deals ÷ signed contracts. The gap shows how many deals fall out after signing.
Cost per appointment
Campaign spend ÷ seller appointments set from that campaign. Closer to real channel cost than cost per lead. In a CRM: One of the Monday 5 .
Cost per contract
Campaign spend ÷ purchase contracts signed from that campaign's leads.
Cost per deal
Campaign spend ÷ closed deals from that campaign. The number that decides whether a channel pays for itself. In a CRM: See the cost per deal calculator .
Cost per lead (CPL)
Campaign spend ÷ leads generated. Easy to measure but misleading on its own, because lead quality varies by channel.
Deal leak
Profit lost between paying for a seller lead and keeping a closed deal: unanswered calls, leads with no next step, offers made off-formula, and fall-outs still counted in ROI. The Kept-Deal Map breaks it into five leak points. In a CRM: Measured with lead source carried to closing, missed-call and next-task reports, and ROI on kept deals.
Disposition (dispo)
Selling or assigning a contracted property to an end buyer. The dispo team markets deals to a cash buyers list.
Double close
Two back-to-back closings: the wholesaler buys the property and immediately resells it, instead of assigning the contract.
Drip / follow-up sequence
Scheduled calls, texts or emails to sellers who aren't ready yet. Most deals come from follow-up, not first contact. In a CRM: Tasks or cadences triggered by lead status and next follow-up date.
Kept deal
A property the investor keeps (for example as a rental) instead of selling. Leaving these out of ROI undercounts the channel that found them. In a CRM: A flag plus a profit value so it counts in campaign ROI.
Lead queue / round robin
A shared list of new leads assigned to reps in rotation or by rules (market, source, availability) so no lead sits unowned.
MAO (maximum allowable offer)
The highest contract price that still leaves room for the end buyer's margin and the wholesaler's fee. Common formula: ARV × 70% − repairs − fee. In a CRM: See the MAO calculator .
Missed-call alert
An automatic task and notification when a call to a marketing number goes unanswered, so someone calls back within minutes.
Motivated seller
An owner with a reason to sell quickly or as-is: inheritance, divorce, relocation, financial distress, a tired landlord, or a property in poor condition.
Pay per lead (PPL)
Buying seller leads from a vendor at a fixed price per lead, instead of paying for ads or mail directly.
PPC (pay per click)
Search or social ads where you pay per click, usually pointed at a seller landing page.
Seventy percent rule (70% rule)
A flipper's rule of thumb: pay no more than 70% of ARV minus repairs. Markets vary, often 65–80%.
Skip tracing
Finding current phone numbers and emails for property owners from public and commercial data, mostly for cold calling and texting.
Speed to lead
The time from a seller reaching out to a real person on your team responding. In a CRM: Measured from lead created time to first logged call.
Transaction coordinator (TC)
The person who manages a deal from signed contract to closing: title, documents, deadlines and communication. In a CRM: A transactions board with stages and required checklist items.
Underwriting
Checking a deal's numbers (ARV, repairs, MAO, exit strategy) before making or accepting an offer. In a CRM: Underwriting fields and a QC gate on the opportunity.
CRM and Salesforce terms
The technical words that come up when you set up or connect a real estate CRM, each linked to the guide that goes deeper.
A2P 10DLC
US registration system for business texts sent from regular 10-digit numbers. Senders register a brand and a campaign through their texting provider. Texting guide →
API access
Permission for other software to read and write Salesforce data. Included in Enterprise and Unlimited; an add-on for Professional. Many integrations need it. Edition guide →
AppExchange
Salesforce’s marketplace of installable apps and integrations, such as DocuSign or dialer packages. Integrations →
Approval process
A rule that routes a record to a manager before it can move on, for example an offer above MAO. Automation features →
Assignment rule
Ordered rules that set a new lead’s owner automatically, by market, source or rotation. Lead routing →
Buy box
A cash buyer’s criteria: zip codes, price range, property types and condition. Stored on the buyer record so deals can be matched. Cash buyers list →
Custom object
A record type you define yourself in Salesforce, such as Property, Offer or Buyer. Data model →
Dead reason
A required picklist explaining why a lead or deal died, so you can tell bad leads from bad follow-up. Field kit →
Duplicate rule
A rule that alerts or blocks when a new record matches an existing one, like the same seller from two lead sources. Data quality →
Express written consent
Documented permission to send marketing texts. CTIA’s messaging guidance calls for it before promotional texts. Texting guide →
Field history tracking
Salesforce’s log of old value, new value, who and when for chosen fields, such as stage or lead source. Data quality →
Flow
Salesforce’s automation tool. Runs when records change, on a schedule, or as guided screens. Automations →
GCLID
Google Click ID. Stored on the lead so Google Ads can learn which clicks became contracts. Lead sources →
Integration user
A dedicated Salesforce login for one integration, with only the permissions it needs. Before you connect →
Junction object
A record linking two others many-to-many, such as which buyers were sent which property. Data model →
Lead source
Where a lead came from: list, mailer, PPC, referral. Should be a picklist set automatically and kept to the closed deal. Lead sources →
Open CTI
The Salesforce framework many dialers use to show inside Salesforce. Salesforce says it reaches end of life on February 28, 2028. Dialer guide →
Opt-out
A seller’s request to stop texts or calls (for example replying STOP). Stored on the record and respected by every tool. Texting guide →
Path
A stage bar on a Salesforce record with key fields and guidance for each stage. Data quality →
Permission set
A bundle of Salesforce permissions added to a user, for example letting VAs create leads without seeing deal financials. Security →
Picklist
A field with fixed choices. Used for lead source, call outcome and dead reason so reports work. Field kit →
Queue
A shared bucket of records that team members claim from, such as hot seller callbacks. Routing →
Reporting snapshot
A saved copy of a report’s results on a schedule, so you can chart trends like weekly pipeline value. Monday 5 →
Roll-up summary field
A field on a parent record that counts or sums its children, such as offers per property. Data model →
Sandbox
A copy of your Salesforce org for testing changes before they reach the team. Health check →
Validation rule
A rule that blocks saving a record until required data is entered, such as timeline and reason on a warm lead. Handoff checklist →
Web-to-Lead
Salesforce’s built-in way to turn website form submissions into leads, up to 500 a day. Lead sources →

## Wholesaling CRM: What It Must Track, Stage by Stage
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesaling-crm.html

Wholesaling CRM: what it must track, stage by stage.
A wholesaling CRM earns its cost when it shows where deals leak between the marketing dollar and the closing table. Check yours against five stages: spend, answer, follow-up, offer and keep. Each stage needs a few required fields, one or two automations, and one number you review every Monday.
The checklist
1. Spend: Know what each closed deal cost
☐ Lead source and campaign on every lead, required ☐ Monthly spend per campaign ☐ Source carried through to the closed deal Monday number: Cost per kept deal by campaign
2. Answer: Talk to sellers before another investor does
☐ Missed calls create the lead and a callback task ☐ Routing to the next available rep ☐ Lead created time and first conversation time Monday number: Median speed to lead; missed calls not returned
3. Follow-up: Keep warm sellers from going quiet
☐ Lead temperature and next follow-up date, required ☐ A dated cadence by temperature ☐ Dead reason plus a date to revisit Monday number: Leads with no next step; follow-ups overdue
4. Offer: Same deal, same math, every rep
☐ ARV, repairs, rule %, fee on the deal ☐ MAO as a formula field ☐ Offer amount and date Monday number: Offers made; offers below MAO
5. Keep: Contracts that actually close
☐ Contract and closing dates ☐ Exit type: assignment or double close ☐ Fall-out reason when a deal dies Monday number: Kept deals; fall-out rate and reasons
Every field above, with picklist values and automation rules, is in the free CRM field kit . To score your current setup in two minutes, take the Deal Leak Score .
How to choose: spreadsheet, investor CRM or Salesforce
Spreadsheet
Fine for one person and a handful of deals. It breaks when several people work leads, when missed calls must become tasks on their own, or when you need cost per closed deal without rebuilding it each month.
An investor CRM
Built for wholesaling and quick to start, with dialers, texting and pipelines included. Check it against the checklist above before you buy, especially lead source carried to the closed deal and fall-out reasons.
Salesforce
More setup, but it fits teams with their own process, several markets or custom reporting, and it grows with the business. I build on Salesforce, so weigh that: the checklist matters more than the brand.
Questions
What is a wholesaling CRM?
The system a wholesaler uses to track sellers, properties, offers, contracts and cash buyers from the first call to the closed assignment or double close. A good one also ties every closed deal back to the marketing that produced it.
What is the most important thing a wholesaling CRM tracks?
Lead source, kept all the way to the closed deal. Without it you cannot tell which campaign paid for which deal, so you cannot cut the ones that lose money.
Is a spreadsheet enough?
For one person doing a few deals it can be. It breaks when more than one person works leads, when missed calls need to become tasks automatically, or when you need cost per closed deal by campaign without rebuilding it by hand.
Should I use an investor CRM or Salesforce?
Investor CRMs come set up for wholesaling and are quicker to start. Salesforce takes setup but fits teams that need their own process, several markets, or custom reporting. I build on Salesforce, so weigh my view with that in mind: the checklist on this page matters more than the brand.
How do I check my current CRM?
Go stage by stage through the checklist on this page and mark each line yes or no. The free Deal Leak Score does the same in ten questions and gives a score out of 100.

## Wholesaling MAO Calculator (70% Rule, Fee, Spread)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/wholesaling-mao-calculator.html

Wholesaling MAO calculator.
Maximum allowable offer from after-repair value, repairs, your assignment fee and your buyer's costs. Change the percentage to match your market. Add your offer price to see the spread.
How MAO works
What is MAO in real estate wholesaling?
MAO (maximum allowable offer) is the highest price you can put a property under contract for and still leave room for your end buyer's profit and your own fee. The common starting formula is ARV × 70% − repair costs − your wholesale fee.
What is the 70% rule?
A rule of thumb used by fix-and-flip buyers: pay no more than 70% of the after-repair value minus repairs. The 30% covers the buyer's holding, selling and financing costs plus profit. Many markets use 65% to 80% depending on price point and competition, so treat it as a dial, not a law.
Should the wholesale fee come out of MAO?
Yes. Your end buyer's number is ARV × % − repairs. Your fee sits on top of your contract price, so your own maximum offer is the buyer's number minus your fee.
Where should ARV and repair numbers come from?
ARV from recent sold comps of similar, renovated properties nearby. Repairs from a walkthrough with a contractor or a repair estimate sheet, plus a contingency. The calculator is only as good as these two inputs.
How do teams keep MAO consistent across acquisition reps?
Put underwriting on the deal record in the CRM: ARV, repair estimate, rule percentage and fee as fields, MAO as a formula, and a required check that comps and repairs were reviewed before the deal moves forward.
